title: Rethinking the Frequency of UN Climate Summits After COP31
summary: Africa: Rethinking the Frequency of UN Climate Summits After COP31 - allAfrica.com Africa: Rethinking the Frequency of UN Climate Summits After COP31 Heads of States after their group photo during the UN Climate Change Conference (file phot
content:
Africa: Rethinking the Frequency of UN Climate Summits After COP31 - allAfrica.com
Africa: Rethinking the Frequency of UN Climate Summits After COP31
Heads of States after their group photo during the UN Climate Change Conference (file photo)
As world leaders and critical stakeholders converge on Türkiye for the 31st UN climate summit, a difficult but necessary question hangs over the familiar ritual. The poser is: after more than three decades, is an annual COP still the best way to advance the global climate agenda?
The two-week conference opening on November 9 in Antalya will gather presidents, diplomats, scientists and activists to bring the climate emergency into sharp focus. Nearly 100 agenda items have been tabled for negotiations, ranging from climate finance and adaptation to loss and damage and energy transition.
I watched that familiar choreography up close at COP29 in Baku in 2024 – the endless pavilions, the late-night huddles over bracketed text, the stirring speeches about urgency followed by painstaking negotiations over wording. It was a powerful reminder of both the value and the limits of these gatherings.
But beyond the elegant speeches and communiques, we must ask whether the annual frequency of the summits has become a substitute for effectiveness. The case for moving from annual to biennial summits is not a call to retreat. Far from it. It is a plea for a more strategic, cost-effective and results-driven model of climate governance.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
Success should be measured not by how often governments meet as output, but by how faithfully their pledges translate into cleaner air, safer communities and more resilient economies in places like Borno, Turkana, the Mekong Delta or the Amazon Basin as outcome. That conversation on the frequency of the summit deserves space at COP31, even if outside the formal negotiating rooms, for many reasons.
First is cost, and the burden is no longer just an African story. Hosting a COP is a massive logistical undertaking: security, accommodation, transport and conference infrastructure for 40,000 to 80,000 participants. The UK spent an estimated 300 million pounds to host COP26 in Glasgow. For any host, it is a fiscal stretch.
For African economies already juggling debt distress, food insecurity and energy poverty, the bill can be prohibitive. It also explains why, despite bearing some of the harshest consequences of the climate crisis, Africa has hosted the summit only five times in 30 years – COP7 in Marrakech in 2001, COP12 in Nairobi in 2006, COP17 in Durban in 2011, COP22 in Marrakech in 2016, and COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022.
The same hosting fatigue is felt elsewhere. Small Island Developing States, which face an existential threat from rising sea level, have never hosted a COP due to scale and cost. Latin America, home to the Amazon, has hosted only three times. When the venue rotates, the Global South often has to build a temporary city from scratch.
Then there is the carbon cost, which is becoming hard to ignore. A 2026 study in Communications Sustainability estimated that air travel by Party and Observer delegates from COP1 to COP29 generated about 710,282 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. More telling is the quantum trajectory: from 2,959 tonnes in Berlin in 1995 to 76,931 tonnes in Baku last year, an increase of roughly 2,500 percent!
Those figures do not capture the full footprint of the summits, but they reveal an uncomfortable paradox that delegates themselves whisper about in the corridors – thousands boarding long-haul flights to discuss how to reduce emissions. A biennial rhythm would halve the frequency of these mega-gatherings and create room for more virtual consultations, regional climate weeks from Africa to Asia-Pacific, and leaner forms of engagement.
There is also the question of implementation. Climate action needs time, and the most vulnerable need even more of it. The annual cycle leaves ministries in a near-permanent state of negotiation. Pledges made in November are barely converted into national budgets and sub-national projects before the next round of talks begins.
We see this at home. Recent floods in Nigeria displaced over a million people. Lake Chad has shrunk by more than 90 percent since the 1960s, deepening conflict between farmers and herders across sub-Sahara Africa. The Sahel is heating 1.5 times faster than the global average.
The pattern is global, and the costs are increasingly human. Global climate impacts now include catastrophic events such as the glacier collapse in Nepal that claimed over 1,000 lives with about 5,000 missing, and extreme heat in Europe linked to tens of thousands of excess deaths. In Pakistan, the 2022 floods caused over 30 billion dollars in damages before its recovery plan could be fully funded by the next COP.
In Brazil, deforestation rates in the Amazon fluctuate faster than annual finance pledges can track. In Vanuatu and Tuvalu, leaders travel each year to plead for survival, yet the Loss and Damage fund agreed at COP27 took another two years to become operational. These are not problems that can be solved between COPs.
A two-year interval would change the incentive. Delegates would return not with a fresh set of promises, but with evidence: how much of the long-promised climate finance actually reached adaptation in Africa, how many hectares of the Great Green Wall were planted, how many communities in Southeast Asia have embraced energy transition, and how many homes in Florida or the Philippines were retrofitted for resilience. That would shift COP from a stage for declarations to a platform for accountability.
Finally, there is credibility. When annual summits end with familiar hollow language and thin follow-through, public fatigue sets in. In Baku, participants listened to the chilling tales of young activists from Kenya and Indonesia who had travelled 48 hours by bus and plane to be there. Their frustration was palpable: "We come every year, but the floods still come every year too."
That fatigue is now visible across continents. Polls in Europe show declining trust that COP pledges will be met. In the US, cities like Phoenix and Miami are spending billions on heat and flood adaptation while federal negotiating positions shift with each election cycle. Communities losing homes in Maiduguri, harvests in Malawi or fishing grounds in Fiji are not waiting for another declaration; they are waiting for irrigation, crop insurance, early warning systems and resilient infrastructure.

Spacing the major conferences two years apart could restore a sense of occasion and scrutiny. Media coverage would be less routine, assessment by environmental rights advocacy groups would be more substantive, and the political cost of empty promises more palpable. The intervening year should not be a pause, but an accountability window.
This does not mean switching off climate diplomacy every other year. Technical negotiations must continue. The UNFCCC already has the architecture for annual synthesis reports, implementation reviews and regional climate weeks. What changes is not the continuity of work, but the frequency of the grand summit.
Yes, critics will worry that a biennial COP could sap momentum. That concern is valid, but urgency should compel better action, not simply more meetings. The UNFCCC has been indispensable in keeping climate on the global agenda. But no institution should be exempt from asking whether its operating model still fits the challenge it was built to address.
COP31 offers more than a negotiating deadline. It offers a moment to ask how we can make climate diplomacy work better for those who need it most. We all need it.

Somalia: Somali Opposition Accuses President of Using Force to Seize Supreme Court
Mogadishu, Somalia — Somalia's opposition coalition, the Somali Future Council, has accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of using security forces to take control of the country's Supreme Court, escalating a political confrontation over the independence of the judiciary and the president's mandate.
The council, led by former president Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and comprising several former Somali leaders, issued a statement condemning what it described as an assault on the Federal Supreme Court and an attempt by Mohamud to seize control of the country's highest judicial institution.
The opposition group also accused security agencies of intimidating former Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed and judges who issued a ruling challenging the terms of the country's federal institutions.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
"The Somali Future Council strongly condemns the assault and coup against the Federal Supreme Court," the statement said, describing the developments as an attack on judicial independence.
The council welcomed the Supreme Court's decision, identified as MS/DST/1/2026, which ruled that the mandates of the president, parliament and federal government had expired.
The court also called on political leaders to agree on an electoral framework within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, according to the ruling.
The judgment directly challenges the government's position that constitutional amendments approved by parliament in March allow Mohamud and federal lawmakers to remain in office until 2027.
The Supreme Court ruled that the amendments extending presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years could not be applied retrospectively to the current officeholders.
The council described the judgment as an opportunity to end the country's political deadlock and resolve disagreements over the electoral process through an inclusive political agreement.
It said Somalia was facing a critical political situation and urged national leaders to respect the court's decision and pursue negotiations to prevent further instability.
The dispute intensified after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed on November 4 and appointed his predecessor, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman, to replace him.
The Supreme Court subsequently declared the dismissal null and void, saying the president had failed to follow the constitutional procedures required to remove the chief justice. It also accused the presidency of attempting to interfere with a pending constitutional case.
The presidency had justified Baashe's removal by citing complaints from judges, judicial staff and legal professionals about the administration of justice and the need for judicial reforms.
In its statement, the Somali Future Council urged citizens to remain vigilant, warning of what it described as serious threats to the country's stability, population and statehood.

The opposition coalition also placed responsibility for the escalating political crisis on Mohamud, accusing him of being at the centre of the dispute.
It warned that the president would bear responsibility for any consequences arising from the situation.
The confrontation comes amid a broader dispute between the federal government and opposition leaders over constitutional amendments, electoral arrangements and the future of Somalia's political transition.
The government has maintained that the constitutional changes provide a legal basis for its electoral roadmap, which schedules parliamentary elections for April 2027 and a presidential vote in May.
Opposition leaders, including the Somali Future Council, have rejected the government's approach and called for an inclusive political agreement on elections.
The latest developments have raised concerns about judicial independence and the potential for further political instability in a country already facing security challenges from Al-Shabaab militants.
The federal government had not immediately responded to the opposition council's latest accusations.

加州一家名为 Machina 的机器人公司获得了 900 万美元的奖励，用于开发集装箱系统，以机器人方式批量生产接近需求点的低成本无人作战攻击系统 (LUCAS) 机身。正如 TWZ 经常指出的那样，LUCAS 无人机以及类似的单向攻击武器在美国作战行动和军事规划中发挥着越来越重要的作用。 Machina 的获奖是五角大楼推动使用集装箱式 3D 打印和其他更靠近前线的先进制造系统的最新例子，以缩短在重大冲突中可能严重退化的供应链。无人机的分散生产还使各单位能够更加灵活，并可以随时根据自己的特定需求定制自己的生产。例如，一个单元可以生产最适合即将到来的任务的多种设计变体，而不必使用它们所运送的任何东西。 Machina 创始人兼首席执行官 Ed Mehr 周五下午对 TWZ 表示，国防部有机工业基础现代化挑战赛的这份为期 18 个月的合同要求 Machina 证明其可以利用其 RoboCraftsman 系统在部署地点制造 LUCAS 无人机。在许多其他地区大规模生产它们的决定将在稍后做出。在爱德华兹空军基地进行飞行测试期间，由 Machina 的 RoboCraftsman 系统创建的 LUCAS 无人机六英尺半比例测试模型。
(Machina) 使用 3D 打印和其他先进制造技术进行无人机和组件的集装箱化生产是一个新兴行业。Machina 系统是围绕这一概念构建的快速增长的功能之一，尽管许多功能都专注于小型无人机。梅尔说，最初，该计划要求 Machina 在美国大陆的两个地点建立所谓的“边缘工厂”。然而，最终目标是能够将它们部署到科威特等国家的转发地点。梅尔告诉我们，边缘工厂由该公司的集装箱式 RoboCraftsman 制造单元组成。这是一个 20 英尺 x 36 英尺的系统，完全安装后重 120,000 磅，本质上是两个机械臂，根据各种要求使用还原制造方法用金属形成机身。有效负载重量、范围和其他因素被输入 nTop 公司设计的软件系统中，然后机械臂根据所需的规格将金属切割成所需的形状因数。 Machina 使用金属而不是许多无人机所用的复合材料，因为“它不仅更便宜，而且用途更广泛，而且现在可以使用像我们这样的自动化工艺进行加工，而复合材料都是通过手工铺层完成的，”Mehr 解释道。

【原文 English Original】
A California robotics company called Machina has been issued a $9 million award for a containerized system to robotically mass-produce Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) airframes close to the point of need. As TWZ has frequently noted , LUCAS drones, and one-way attack weapons like them, are playing an increasing role in U.S. combat operations and military planning. The award to Machina is the latest example of the Pentagon’s push to use containerized 3D printing and other advanced fabricating systems closer to the front lines to shorten supply chains that could get severely degraded in a major conflict. Decentralizing production of drones also allows units to be more flexible and tailor their own production to their specific needs at any given moment. For instance, a unit can produce variations of multiple designs that are best suited to an upcoming mission instead of having to use whatever they are shipped. (Machina) This 18-month contract from the Defense Department’s Organic Industrial Base Modernization Challenge calls for Machina to prove it can build LUCAS drones at deployed locations with its RoboCraftsman system, Ed Mehr, founder and CEO of Machina, told TWZ Friday afternoon. A decision on producing them at scale in many other locales will come later. A LUCAS drone six-foot half-scale test model created by Machina’s RoboCraftsman system during a flight test at Edwards Air Force Base. (Machina) Creating containerized production of drones and components using 3D printing and other advanced manufacturing techniques at the forward edge is a burgeoning industry. The Machina system is one of a rapidly growing number of capabilities built around this concept, although many focus on smaller drones. Building Drones Near The Point Of Need Initially, the plan calls for Machina to set up so-called “Edge Factories” at two locations in the continental United States, said Mehr. However, the ultimate goal is to be able to deploy them to forward locations in countries like Kuwait. The Edge Factories consist of the company’s containerized RoboCraftsman manufacturing cells, Mehr told us. A 20-foot by 36-foot system that weighs 120,000 pounds fully installed, it is essentially two robotic arms that form the airframe out of metal using reductive manufacturing based on a variety of requirements. Payload weight, range and other factors are punched into a software system designed by the nTop company and the robotic arms then cut the metal into the desired form factor based on the required specifications. Machina uses metal instead of composites that many drones are made out of because “not only it is cheaper, it is more widely available and now can be processed with an automated process like ours versus composites, which are all done by hand layup ,” Mehr explained. The following Machina video shows how the RoboCraftsman system, guided by the inputs, forms the metal to craft the airframe. This avoids having to use equipment like dies and rolls, dramatically speeding the process and allowing production at scale, Mehr stated. “Basically, the agentic AI agents can explore and generate whole different versions of an airframe with different parameters,” Mehr proffered. “Because now it’s parameterized, you can just change the parameters and you get another airframe, and then evaluate if that airframe is good for the requirement they want.” This way, the RoboCraftsman system “can easily generate 20, 30, 40, 50 different designs just in software, and then put it through simulations to figure out which one actually meets the requirement for that,” the Machina CEO added. “The concept is that we’re going to bring this capability closer to the point of need, so that you can build a different requirement for let’s say PACOM versus U.S. CENTCOM versus in Ukraine,” Mehr said. “They can easily switch and build a drone that they need.” Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) drones in the U.S. Central Command region. (CENTCOM) (U.S. Central Command Public Affairs) Under this contract, each Edge Factory will consist of one or two RoboCraftsman cells and each cell can make a LUCAS airframe in two to five days, depending on the size, Mehr said. A scaled deployment of 10 or more cells would take place under a new contract, he added. The systems can make “anywhere from a one-off all the way to the thousands, sometimes tens of thousands,” Mehr said. It all depends on the number of RoboCraftsman systems that are ordered. At the moment, Mehr envisions that each 12-foot airframe will cost “somewhere around $15,000 to $40,000,” depending on the complexity. This range is a relatively common price point for Russian Shahed-136 variants and U.S. knockoffs under the LUCAS program. The company has already produced a six-foot, half-scale airframe that was recently tested at Edwards Air Force Base, said Mehr. However, that initial test proved problematic. “The first design had some challenges with crosswind mitigation,” Mehr told us. “Since then, we have moved the location of the engine slightly to enable better crosswind mitigation, and now we’re running again. And the beauty is for us to go from one design to the next is just like a couple of months, a maximum of three months. Like we can just then try it again.” A six-foot, half-scale LUCAS drone, made by a Machina RoboCraftsman system, being tested at Edwards Air Force Base, California. (Machina) Mehr said that Machina is not working with SpektreWorks, which designed and made the LUCAS drones previously supplied to the U.S. military and already used in combat. SpektreWorks declined to comment. The Edge Factory contract is one of several Machina has been awarded to use these systems to help build and repair military hardware. In July, Machina was issued a qualification contract by Lockheed Martin to produce fuel tanks for AGM-158 Joint Air-To-Surface Standoff Missiles (JASSM). That plan called for the creation of a 200,000-square-foot facility “designed to house up to 50 RoboCraftsman cells and support high-rate production of mission-critical metal structures for defense programs including JASSM,” according to a media release at the time . “By integrating forming, machining, welding, and assembly under one roof, Machina Factory 3 compresses production timelines from months to days.” “Lockheed Martin Ventures invested in Machina Labs for its powerful combination of speed, flexibility, and scalability, and our teams have worked closely to transition key capabilities to production,” said Chris Moran, vice president and general manager, Lockheed Martin Ventures. “Machina’s work advances capacity, reduces risk, and helps ensure we can deliver mission-critical capabilities at scale. We congratulate Machina on this milestone as a supplier, which further strengthens an innovative and resilient American Defense Industrial Base.” U.S. Air Force Staff Sgt. Seth Blackwood, 363rd Training Squadron Aircraft Armament instructor, directs the installation of an AGM-158 JASSM onto a B-52 during a Combat Capability Demonstration April 16, 2024, at Sheppard Air Force Base, Texas. (U.S. Air Force photo by Rachel Ross) Rachel Ross Earlier this year, a Machina RoboCraftsman platform helped repair a C-17 Globemaster III cargo jet that was damaged during a tornado, Mehr told us. The system “fabricated a first-of-its-kind replacement part for the damaged C-17 without the need for dedicated tooling,” the company noted . “Machina deployed a RoboCraftsman at the RSO [ Rapid Sustainment Office ], where production for a left nose panel began in March 2026 and was completed in May 2026. The aircraft returned to flight on July 30, 2026 at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio.” Damage to a C-17 Globemaster III cargo jet caused by a tornado that was eventually repaired with a Machina RoboCraftsman system. (Machina) We asked the Pentagon for information about why they selected Machina and their metrics for success, but we have not heard back yet. Pentagon Pushing For Deployable Manufacturing The U.S. military has been pushing for several years for the employment of mobile additive and other forms of advanced manufacturing “to produce unmanned aircraft components in remote or austere environments and reduce dependence on traditional supply chains,” the Air Force’s innovation arm, AFWERX, noted last month . The idea is to place these systems in a wide array of locations, produce the quantity needed and tailor the airframe for the mission. In one such case, the Air National Guard and Air Force Special Operations Command partnered with the San Diego-based Firestorm company in 2023 “to create an expeditionary assembly unit capable of mass-producing unmanned aerial systems,” according to the Pentagon . The result was called an Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell or xCell. “It’s basically an expeditionary 3D printer,” Master Sgt. Richard Stone, 194th Air Support Operations Group innovation officer, explained at the time. “The basis of the technology is … it’s about the size of a [shipping container] and it can print out, for this specific use case, drones.” “Inside this [shipping container], it’ll print out all the components,” said Stone “But then you have what’s called RPA, which is robotic process [automation.]” The xCell “prints the individual pieces and then uses RPA to assemble the major components of the drone,” the Pentagon added. A render of Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell or xCell which is capable of mass-producing unmanned aerial systems. Theoretically, xCell can be hidden in plain sight while running on local resources to 3D-print items on the battle field. (Courtesy photo from Firestorm) 194th Wing “The user can take these components and, almost like Legos, put them together,” said Stone. “So if you want a longer drone with a specific payload, you can take those components and put them together and the computer will tell you, ‘This is where the wings go and this is where the center of gravity should be.” The company went on to produce Tempest drones that were flying with 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, during Exercise Balikatan 2026 at Cagayan North International Airport in the Philippines, AFWERX noted. A Firestorm Tempest Drone with 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, is staged for preflight checks during Exercise Balikatan 2026 at Cagayan North International Airport, Lal-Lo, Philippines, April 23, 2026. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Ernesto Lagunes) Cpl. Ernesto Lagunes Our own Jamie Hunter recently interviewed Craig Anders, senior vice president of growth at Aevex, about the company’s ForgeX containerized 3D drone printing system . The ForgeX system “represents being able to take the fight further forward, print drones on demand, print them out towards the front of the lines, cut down the logistics trail, and absolutely revolutionize the battlefield,” said Anders.  The goal is to be “able to kick these planes out the door on short timelines to go out and get the missions done, work within the local area to make sure that the mission can be accomplished by any means necessary,” he added. Anders said the ForgeX printers fabricate three types of drones, the Vandal , Onyx and Raker . He added that the system can produce up to 880 a year. Growing U.S. Reliance On LUCAS The U.S. military first announced it had begun fielding LUCAS, which was reverse-engineered from the Iranian-designed Shahed-136 , in December 2025. This came just months after TWZ laid out a detailed case for why the U.S. military should start acquiring Shahed-136 clones in large volumes. LUCAS made its official combat debut in the opening phases of major combat operations against Iran earlier this year. The pusher-propeller, combustion-engine-powered kamikaze drones were first launched from the ground, a U.S. official told us at the time. They can also be fired from ships. In March, CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper told us the LUCAS drones were “indispensable. ” The following video shows Cooper answering our question about the LUCAS drones. CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper on LUCAS: LUCAS is indispensable. pic.twitter.com/VaLXmjawA6 — Clash Report (@clashreport) March 5, 2026 Now the Army is looking to expand the use of these weapons to the Pacific, Maj. Gen. Bernard Harrington, head of the 7th Infantry Division, told us during the Association of the U.S. Army (AUSA) conference last month. “So we see that playing a key role in order to be able to achieve that effect at mass, … [and] in an affordable manner, while also being able potentially to preserve something that’s more exquisite for something that requires an exquisite munition.” “So as we start modeling out what it looks like to be able to penetrate a portion of the anti-access/area denial network in support of the joint task force in the PACOM [U.S. Pacific Command] area of operations, we started looking at, well, how do I bend – how do I achieve mass at a cost curve?” the 7th Infantry and MDC-PAC commander explained. “What effect am I really trying to achieve on a system in order to provide that window of opportunity for that joint force commander?” A map showing Chinese military outposts in the Spratly Islands at the southern end of the South China Sea. This gives a good sense of the anti-access/area denial bubbles that China has already established and continues to expand upon. (DOD) “So maybe I don’t necessarily need to sink a ship, but if I take out certain systems on that vessel, well then it creates this temporal window opportunity,” he continued. “Then that joint force commander can surge in that carrier strike group or bomber task force.” While the exact details of the LUCAS program requirements have been hard to pin down, it’s likely that multiple drone types from multiple manufacturers could become part of the program as time goes on. Ed Mehr gave us an idea of what that could look like: “Shahed clearly inspired LUCAS, which stands for Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System. But we shouldn’t confuse the inspiration with the destination. The future isn’t about mass-producing replicas of one drone. Different theaters and missions demand different performance, and therefore different designs. That could mean a LUCAS-style drone or a wide variety of Group 2 and Group 3 unmanned aircraft. The real breakthrough is making that diversity affordable. We’re developing flexible manufacturing technologies that can produce many different designs cost-effectively using one of the cheapest and most proven aerospace materials: sheet metal. It’s what aircraft have been built from for generations. We’re bringing it into an era where manufacturing can adapt as quickly as the mission.” We won’t know how the Machina contract ultimately pans out until sometime in mid-2028. Regardless, given the importance of both the LUCAS drones and deployable, additive and advanced manufacturing are becoming, this is likely a first step in what could be a whole new logistics concept that could underpin a significant portion of the growing LUCAS program. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post LUCAS Drones To Be Built In Containerized Robotic Micro Factories Designed To Be Forward Deployed appeared first on TWZ .

title: 中共跨境“反腐” 专家忧其沦为权斗工具
summary: 【大纪元2026年11月08日讯】（大纪元记者程木兰、骆亚采访报导）中共全国人大常委会11月6日通过“反跨境腐败法”，同日生效。北京把海外追逃追赃纳入常设机制，由国家监察委员会统筹，并收紧外方在中国境内调查取证。专家警告，在中共主导查办的体制下，这套机制可被用来追查失势官员的海外资产，也为境外“劝返”和政治施压异议人士提供新名目。 北京把“猎狐”“天网”纳入常设机制 中共于10月26日至29日在北京召开二十届五中全会宣告“全面从严治党”，并有多位官员遭开除党籍。随后于十四届全
content: 【大纪元2026年11月08日讯】（大纪元记者程木兰、骆亚采访报导）中共全国人大常委会11月6日通过“反跨境腐败法”，同日生效。北京把海外追逃追赃纳入常设机制，由国家监察委员会统筹，并收紧外方在中国境内调查取证。专家警告，在中共主导查办的体制下，这套机制可被用来追查失势官员的海外资产，也为境外“劝返”和政治施压异议人士提供新名目。 北京把“猎狐”“天网”纳入常设机制 中共于10月26日至29日在北京召开二十届五中全会宣告“全面从严治党”，并有多位官员遭开除党籍。随后于十四届全国人大常委会第二十五次会议11月6日表决通过《反跨境腐败法》，公布之日起施行。 中国问题专家王赫接受大纪元采访时指出，防堵资金外流，尤其是防止国有资产藉利益输送流往境外，是北京扩大追查权的一个动机。 他分析，过去的“猎狐”“天网”主要靠专案推进。中共这次把分散的涉外规定和部门权责集中起来，由国家监察委员会牵头，让公安、财政、审计和反洗钱部门能在同一机制下共享线索。 资深评论员横河则注意到，新法通过当天即生效，有别于往常惯例。他推测这部法是为了惩罚某个人或某些人，“抓人时还没有足够的法律可用来惩罚，所以急需立新法”。 中国大陆前检察官沈良庆也把立法时点与中共二十届五中全会重申“从严治党”相连，视为这项党内政策的立法配套。他向大纪元表示，中共在缺少引渡协议的地方往往只能逐案协商，既有行动的成效受到限制。 中共新法上路前，当局依《监察法》请求外国协助引渡嫌疑人、追回涉案资产。新法上路后，涉案行为是否构成犯罪，仍按中共《刑法》判断。 据新华社今年2月底转述中纪委工作报告，中共官方2025年立案查处505件跨境腐败案件，并透过“天网”等行动追回963名外逃人员。 反腐法律成为权斗工具？ 王赫用“看人下菜”形容中共的选择性反腐，“不是看你做了什么，是看你是什么样的人。” 他认为，在中共领导反腐工作的架构下，“政治忠诚”和站队仍可能左右谁被立案、谁被保护。对当局有意保护的高官，他担忧海外资产线索可能以机密为由被搁置。对政治对手，北京则能动员更多部门追查资金、寻求境外协助。他预判，新法将“成为权力斗争的一个合法化的工具”。 中国大陆律师章廷（化名）把问题追溯到中共制定法律的方式。他接受大纪元采访时以“帮规”和“家法”形容这套法律，认为立法缺乏民众充分参与和真正授权，制定和执行法律的考量，往往是维持中共统治与保护特权阶层。 他认为，在中共体制下，若案件未牵涉权斗，新法对在任或退休高官及其家属的影响可能有限。 章廷指出，权力缺乏制衡所造成的腐败，很难靠再立一部法律解决。他把这类反腐形容为“清洗的手段，是权斗的延伸”。 沈良庆则把反腐与权斗交织、选择性执法的现象称为“制度性的老大难痼疾”。在他看来，新法对官员及其家属向境外转移涉案资产，或有一定约束，但公权力缺乏制衡的问题始终存在。 高官家属的海外资产能否被追及？ 王赫认为，财政、审计与反洗钱部门共享线索后，当局更容易追查中低层外逃官员及国企高管的资金流向。若资产所在国愿意合作，冻结涉案财产也较有可能。 至于高层官员和家属，他认为新法的约束力“非常有限”。即使财产登记在亲属名下，追缴仍涉及两个关口。中国境内须启动查办并厘清资产与违法所得的关联，境外的查账、冻结或返还则须由当地依法律程序处理。 王赫认为，北京可向关系较密切的国家寻求协助，例如中东或东南亚部分国家，请求冻结涉案资产。横河则强调，外国原本就不愿协助的案件，未必会因北京有了新法而改变立场。 欧洲人权法院2022年曾就波兰拟将一名因被控涉嫌跨国电信诈欺而引渡至中国的嫌疑人，裁定其有遭受不当待遇的实际风险，移交将违反《欧洲人权公约》。国际刑警组织（INTERPOL）也说明，各国是否依红色通报采取逮捕行动，仍依本国法律决定。 北京反制外国调查 跨国企业夹在中间 新法允许北京在认定外国不当行使域外管辖、损害中国利益等条件下采取反制措施，也要求外方在中国境内展开反腐执法调查，以及境内机构向境外提供相关证据或资料，须经中方同意。 沈良庆认为，中共一方面要求出海企业加强合规，另一方面也藉反制条款牵制外国政府调查中国企业及官员。王赫以美国《海外反腐败法》（FCPA）为例指出，若外方要求一家跨国公司提交在中国掌握的文件，公司可能同时面对外方取证要求和中方限制。他形容这是“中美之间司法对抗的一个升级”。 中国民主活动家王丹在播客节目《王丹学堂》也以内部审计为例，指出跨国企业总部若要查核海外交易，而中共监管机关同时以跨境腐败为由要求取得审计资料，当地团队将面临两套要求而难以适从。 反腐名义将被用于跨境施压？ 横河指出，过去有些境外“劝返”透过跟踪、威胁或向境内家属施压，迫使当事人回中国。他担忧，新法会让这类行动更容易被北京包装成反腐执法。 美国司法部2025年4月16日公布，曾参与“猎狐”行动的纽约前警员麦克马洪（Michael McMahon），因非法充当中国政府代理人及跨州跟踪等罪名，被判入狱18个月。 王丹也认为，新法替争议性的境外行动“穿上了一件法律的外衣”。他特别质疑，法律涵盖部分行为发生在境外、结果落在中国境内的同类腐败行为，可能给执法机关留下扩张解释的空间。他以政治捐款、慈善捐款和学术交流为例，追问当局将如何划定正常资金往来与涉案交易的界线。 他担心，当局可能从海外异议人士与境内亲友的资金往来着手，将人列为案件关系人，再借经济调查施压。在王丹看来，这种不确定性，本身就可能造成寒蝉效应。

title: 馮睎乾：黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？
summary: 馮睎乾十三維度 臉書 2026-11-7 黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？ 被指「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全」的黃之鋒，昨日被判囚十年。法官譚耀豪稱黃之鋒、羅冠聰同為主腦，「罪行重大」，判刑須具阻嚇力，並表達「社會對黃之鋒計劃及行為的厭惡」（但社會有多少人厭惡呢？），故以十三年為量刑起點，考慮被告認罪，扣減至監禁十年，其中兩個月零兩日跟「初選案」刑期同時執行。因兩項「国安罪」，三十歲的黃之鋒共須服刑約十四年半，出獄已四十歲了。 黃之鋒究竟犯了什麼大罪，需要重判十年監禁呢
content: 馮睎乾十三維度 臉書  2026-11-7 黃之鋒判刑書是怎樣寫成的？ 被指「串謀勾結外國或者境外勢力危害國家安全」的黃之鋒，昨日被判囚十年。法官譚耀豪稱黃之鋒、羅冠聰同為主腦，「罪行重大」，判刑須具阻嚇力，並表達「社會對黃之鋒計劃及行為的厭惡」（但社會有多少人厭惡呢？），故以十三年為量刑起點，考慮被告認罪，扣減至監禁十年，其中兩個月零兩日跟「初選案」刑期同時執行。因兩項「国安罪」，三十歲的黃之鋒共須服刑約十四年半，出獄已四十歲了。 黃之鋒究竟犯了什麼大罪，需要重判十年監禁呢？宏福苑大火死了168人，政府內那些嚴重瀆職的官吏沒一個坐牢，涉嫌操控「死人授權票」的黃碧嬌仍未被捕，黃之鋒的罪行難道比牠們嚴重？我瀏覽了近萬字的判刑書，想看看黃之鋒幹了什麼傷天害理的壞事，到頭來卻發現唯一的「罪證」，主要集中在判詞第35段，原來就是轉發羅冠聰的臉書貼文。 第35段列出黃之鋒九大「犯罪行為」，出現最頻密的字眼就是「The post was shared by the defendant on his Facebook page on the same day」，即「被告同日將該貼文轉載至他的臉書專頁」——「該貼文」是指羅冠聰的貼文。據判詞說，2020年7月至10月間，羅到英、美呼籲制裁中国及香港，並發起請願要求以色列公司Cellebrite停止向港警供應情報產品，黃則轉發相關貼文。 但光是轉發貼文，有必要判一個年輕人坐牢十年、毁掉他的大好青春嗎？或許連譚耀豪也覺得太欠缺說服力，所以必須把被告寫得更像個滿腹陰謀的「主腦」才行。怎寫呢？最麻煩的是，控方花五年蒐證，根本證明不到有任何外國組織或資金支持被告（見判詞第55段）。跟黎智英一樣，黃之鋒多年來被指「收美國佬錢」，如今經香港警方「fact check」，證實都是子虛烏有。 不知道譚耀豪思索多久，才想通怎樣扣黃之鋒的帽子。但他最後也勉強交到功課。譚在第35段指，當羅冠聰呼籲外國對港實施制裁、封鎖或敵對措施時，「被告的角色就是在香港提供『地下』支援（the defendant’s role was to provide his “underground” support in Hong Kong）」，引起外國關注，增強呼籲效果。譚耀豪為「underground」一字加上引號，似乎是因為他引用了黃之鋒2020年8月在英國《衛報》發表的一篇文章。 我查看該文，黃之鋒是這樣寫的： When certain slogans and songs are forbidden, the city’s protesters use wordplay, songs with Morse code messages, and blank sticky notes to express our grievances. Others even subvert the Chinese Communist party’s own dogma, or the first line of the Chinese anthem “Arise, ye who refuse to be slaves”. Since political organisations are the primary targets of the law, resistance must now go underground, with some, like Nathan Law, fleeing the city to keep speaking out in the international arena. （當某些口號和歌曲被禁，此城的示威者便改以文字遊戲、暗藏摩斯密碼訊息的歌曲，以及空白便利貼來表達不滿。有人甚至反過來挪用中共自身的教條，或国歌的首句「起來，不願做奴隸的人們」，藉此表達抗爭。由於政治組織是這條法律的主要打擊目標，抵抗運動如今只能轉入地下，部分人士則如羅冠聰那樣，逃離香港，繼續在國際舞台上發聲。） 只要不是斷章取義，任何人都明白黃之鋒所謂「go underground」，顯然是呼應前面所述的各種隱微的表達不滿的方式，即港府常常掛在嘴邊的「軟對抗」（不犯法的），而非暗示什麼驚天動地的大陰謀。問題是，判詞列舉的所有「罪行」，其實沒一項符合「underground」定義；也就是說，法庭根本從未證明黃之鋒為羅冠聰提供了任何「地下」支援。 眾所周知，「underground」是秘密的、不見光的，但黃之鋒的「罪行」全是在社交平台公開發布或轉發文章，光明正大，怎可能稱為「underground」呢？但欲加之罪既已無辭，譚耀豪為了交差，已懶理是否自相矛盾，就斷章取義抽出黃之鋒某篇文某個字，霸王硬上弓指黃轉發貼文，就是為羅冠聰提供「地下」支援，胡亂用一個引號便僭建罪名，彷彿兩人真有許多不見得光的勾當。 在正常法治社會，就算像羅冠聰那樣做國際遊說，公開呼籲外國政府向自己的國家施壓，也是合情合理合法的，何況僅僅是轉發貼文？去年9月英國改革黨黨魁法拉奇（Nigel Farage）赴美國國會作證，批評英國《網絡安全法》打壓言論自由，促請美國運用外交及貿易手段向英國施壓。時任英揆施紀賢批評法拉奇唱衰英國，甚至指他遊說美國制裁英國，直斥他不愛國。法拉奇否認要求正式制裁，但承認主張利用經濟及貿易槓桿，迫使英國改變政策。 羅冠聰所做的，和法拉奇差不多，英國政府有出動國安法把法拉奇收監嗎？沒有。如果黃之鋒真的有「罪」，那肯定不是唱衰香港，或支持那些被港官視為「不痛不癢」（曾國衛語）、「一笑置之，嗤之以鼻」（林鄭月娥語）、「完全沒有當是一回事」（鄧炳強語）的制裁，而是他把「国安法」實施後的香港看得太美好了，誤以為自己只要光明磊落，做一些全世界法治社會都合法的事，那就必定不會有問題。 黃之鋒「犯法」時，應該不知道自己正「犯法」，更想不到要重判十年。譚耀豪在第56段寫了一句，是判詞中少數我覺得有理的話：「被告唯一沒意識到的，就是他轉發LKC（羅冠聰）呼籲實施制裁的訊息這一行為，可以被用作證據，證明他與LKC及其他人串謀（The only thing that the defendant did not realize was that his acts of sharing LKC’s messages calling for sanctions could be used as evidence to prove his conspiracy with LKC and others）。」 轉發臉書貼文，居然是導致十年監禁的「串謀證據」，試問除了能夠百分百釘死被告的国安法官外，還有誰意識得到呢？ 相關文章 黃之鋒犯了什麼罪？ https://www.patreon.com/sefirot/posts/16850473 6

title: 澳门首宗国安案：澳门前民主派立法会议员区锦新获刑12年6个月
summary: （维权网信息中心报道） 2026 年 11 月 7 日，本网获悉：澳门首宗国安案：澳门前民主派立法会议员区锦新获刑 12 年 6 个月。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，澳门法院裁定 69 岁的区锦新五项罪名成立，包括“颠覆国家政权罪”、“与境外组织联系危害国家安全”及“违反保密罪”。 案件于 9 月闭门审理。区锦新自 2025 年 7 月被捕后一直被羁押。其家属此前表示，近一年无法与他联系，也无法自行委托辩护律师。 区锦新简历 ： 1957 年 4 月 30 日出生，葡萄牙
content: （维权网信息中心报道） 2026 年 11 月 7 日，本网获悉：澳门首宗国安案：澳门前民主派立法会议员区锦新获刑 12 年 6 个月。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，澳门法院裁定 69 岁的区锦新五项罪名成立，包括“颠覆国家政权罪”、“与境外组织联系危害国家安全”及“违反保密罪”。 案件于 9 月闭门审理。区锦新自 2025 年 7 月被捕后一直被羁押。其家属此前表示，近一年无法与他联系，也无法自行委托辩护律师。 区锦新简历 ： 1957 年 4 月 30 日出生，葡萄牙语名 Au Kam San ，祖籍广东新兴县，原葡属澳门籍、现中华人民共和国（澳门）和葡萄牙双国籍人，原为澳门青洲小学教师，后为知名社运人士，前“新澳门学社”创会成员，前澳门民主发展联委会理事长，“澳门小区发展新动力”会员大会副主席，澳门立法会议员，澳门民主派核心人物，中国在押政治犯。 自幼生长于澳门；大学时期，曾在澳门东亚大学攻读社会科学学士，毕业后又在中国大陆华南师范大学修读教育硕士；学成返回澳门，曾在澳门青洲小学任职教师； 1989 年，中国大陆发生八九民运，澳门有多个团体发起游行及各种声援行动，其因积极参与其中并加入论政团体“民主沙龙”（后更名为澳门民主发展联委会，简称民联会），但六四事件过后，其等多名民主派人士因受到诸如职业威胁、家庭压力和街头暴力袭击等多重压力而被迫辞职或被解雇，以致于民联会除其与吴国昌之外，成员多都四散；后其二人先后从政，透过直选而进入立法会，但其二人仍坚持举办六四悼念集会，直到该集会被中共澳门当局禁止； 1993 年，其开始担任澳门市政议员，四年以后，其又在澳门回归后连续 20 年担任五届立法会议员，直至 2021 年立法会选举宣布不寻求连任；在参加社运活动方面， 1992 年 7 月，其因与吴国昌等人成立民主派团体新澳门学社，以“立足于澳门，研究澳门社会状况，推动本地区现代化发展”为宗旨，以专业知识研究澳门社会的各方面议题，并充分利用立法会议员的权力，围绕澳门民生问题及政府施政失误提出了多个议案和反映市民的要求，故广泛得到民众支持，使该学社成为澳门最重要的民主派社团之一；数年后，新澳门学社内部因主张积极参与社运的“少壮派”与议会路线的“元老派”发生纷争，遂其于 2016 年 1 月致函学社会内，以“学社背离当年创办宗旨信念”为由退出了该社团组织，后又另组政党“澳门小区发展新动力”，并于次年成功连任立法会议员； 2018 年 9 月，其因就惹起外界疑虑的《通讯截取及保障法律制度》公开咨询接受媒体访问，质疑警方对他作出监听行为疑超越法律，认为“按法律，警方若监听电话，须先获法官批准”，并认为虽支持警方加强监督机制，但须有调查实权才能发挥作用，故而其言论被澳门保安司司长不点名指责，称其相关言论是“信口雌黄、胡乱猜测、犯诽谤罪”；后因其言论遭警方追究刑事责任，成为澳门回归后首例，故此事在坊间及网上迅速引起热议，人们均反感司警对事件的处理手法，几乎一面倒批评该做法不合理，同时也触动了对当地政府的不满情绪；针此，就有时事评论员指说，公众其实更有需要关注“在法律上如何健全监察机制和信息透明，以确保公众知情权和市民隐私等问题”； 2021 年 4 月 8 日，在立法会全体会议上，其因提及全国人大常委会通过修改香港有关选举制度，是在“摧毁香港民主普选制度”，故在发言提出后，就被施家伦、陈虹、崔世平等 5 名议员要求解释并收回言论，认为其所言片面，无视香港有人以分裂国家的方式争取民主； 2021 年，其因受压力而宣布不参加立法会选举（实因被指不效忠澳门特区被取消参选资格），至此结束其 20 年的立法会直选议员生涯。 2025 年 7 月 30 日，其突然被澳门司法警察局以涉嫌违反澳门《国安法》第 13 条“与澳门特别行政区以外的组织、团体或个人建立联系作出危害国家安全的行为罪”逮捕，次日移交检察院侦办；其被指控，“自从 2022 年起就涉嫌勾连多个境外反华组织，向对方提供大量不实且具煽动性的数据，作为境外及网上持续公开展览之用”，并在澳门《国安法》 2023 年生效后，还继续使用有关数据，以“协助他人收集或公然散布虚假及明显歪曲的消息等方式，引发他人对中国中央人民政府的仇恨、促成反华势力采取对中国及澳门特区的敌对行动，以及破坏澳门特区选举，严重危害国家安全”；其遭逮捕时，家也遭搜查，部分书籍被搜走，其妻子郑妙珊亦被带走，后被列为其案证人；针此，欧盟对外行动署立刻于同年 8 月 2 日发布声明，谴责澳门政府将其逮捕，批评此举加深了外界对澳门政治多元性和言论自由受侵蚀的担忧。 2026 年 11 月 6 日，澳门法院裁定 69 岁的区锦新五项罪名成立，包括“颠覆国家政权罪”、“与境外组织联系危害国家安全”及“违反保密罪”。案件于 9 月闭门审理。区锦新自 2025 年 7 月被捕后一直被羁押。其家属此前表示，近一年无法与他联系，也无法自行委托辩护律师。目前被羁押在澳门看守所。

title: Hybrid War Makes High North a Contest for NATO
zh_title: 混合战争使高北地区成为北约的竞争
summary: 本文是关于北极新战略格局的 CEPA 系列的一部分。 “高北，低紧张”正在成为一个令人安慰的口号，而不是一个可信的策略。俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争、北约的北扩以及俄中合作的不断发展削弱了北极例外论。俄罗斯与北约的常规战争并非不可避免，但莫斯科可能会继续利用破坏、网络攻击、电子干扰和挑衅来挑战主权并考验盟国的决心。联盟面临的挑战是保卫高北地区免受故意保留的侵略
content:
本文是关于北极新战略格局的 CEPA 系列的一部分。 “高北，低紧张”正在成为一个令人安慰的口号，而不是一个可信的策略。俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争、北约的北扩以及俄中合作的不断发展削弱了北极例外论。俄罗斯与北约的常规战争并非不可避免，但莫斯科可能会继续利用破坏、网络攻击、电子干扰和挑衅来挑战主权并考验盟国的决心。该联盟面临的挑战是保卫高北地区免受故意控制在战争门槛以下的侵略。莫斯科的北极战略的核心是保护其核威慑力量、控制北方航道以及限制北约进入俄罗斯敏感领土。科拉半岛毗邻挪威和芬兰，是主要北方舰队和海基核资产的所在地，是实现这些目标的核心。乌克兰战争削弱了俄罗斯的一些常规能力，而芬兰和瑞典的加入北约则增强了莫斯科的暴露感，这两者的结合可能会鼓励俄罗斯更加依赖非对称行动。莫斯科还渴望通过在其他地方施加压力来转移西方对乌克兰的注意力和资源。传统上被削弱的俄罗斯并不一定意味着北极更安全。
原因之一是，距离遥远、气候恶劣和基础设施稀疏，使得莫斯科对北极的破坏难以察觉，而且修复成本高昂。水下电缆尤其脆弱。 9月，北约船只阻止了俄罗斯在斯瓦尔巴群岛附近的一次秘密行动，该行动涉及俄罗斯专门的深海指挥部GUGI和关键的电缆基础设施。涉事船只与北约船只遭遇后，没有收到任何损坏报告，但这一事件表明了战略破坏的可能性。这种威胁还延伸到陆上：针对港口、燃料库、电力基础设施和物流中心的纵火和破坏可能会扰乱民用服务和北约的增援，而使用代理行为者将使归因进一步复杂化。 GPS 干扰、欺骗和网络攻击也具有类似的作用。俄罗斯还可以调整北约东翼使用的战术，包括无人机入侵盟军领空，以测试北极的监视、响应时间和政治决心。北约 2026 年弹性基准要求认识到这些相互关联的漏洞，协调一致的电子、网络和物理攻击可能会放大其后果。研究船、渔船和商业平台也可以为监视或破坏准备提供掩护，关键基础设施周围的可疑行为需要进行审查。
分析人士警告说，敌对国家利用商业和科学行动作为北极威胁活动的掩护。斯瓦尔巴群岛尤其将自然脆弱性与政治压力结合在一起，克里姆林宫正在利用历史叙述、信息行动、海上压力和法律模糊性来挑战挪威的权威。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。电子邮件提交 Δ document.getElementById( "ak_js_2" ).setAttribute( "value", ( new Date() ).getTime() ); gform.initializeOnLoaded( function() {jQuery('#gform_ajax_frame_1').on('load',function(){var content = jQuery(this).contents().find('*').html();var is_postback =contents.indexOf('GF_AJAX_

【原文 English Original】
This article forms part of a CEPA series on the new strategic landscape in the Arctic. “High North, low tension” is becoming a comforting slogan rather than a credible strategy. Russia’s war on Ukraine, NATO’s northern enlargement, and growing Russia-China cooperation have eroded Arctic exceptionalism . A conventional Russia-NATO war is not inevitable, but Moscow is likely to continue using sabotage, cyberattacks, electronic interference, and provocations to challenge sovereignty and test allied resolve. The alliance’s challenge is to defend the High North against aggression deliberately kept below the threshold of war. Moscow’s Arctic strategy centers on protecting its nuclear deterrent, controlling the Northern Sea Route, and restricting NATO’s access to sensitive Russian territory. The Kola Peninsula, which abuts Norway and Finland and is home to key Northern Fleet and sea-based nuclear assets, is central to these objectives. The war in Ukraine has weakened some of Russia’s conventional capabilities, while Finland and Sweden’s NATO accession has heightened Moscow’s sense of exposure , a combination that may encourage greater reliance on asymmetric operations. Moscow is also eager to divert Western attention and resources away from Ukraine by generating pressure elsewhere. A conventionally weakened Russia does not necessarily mean a safer Arctic. One reason is that vast distances, harsh weather, and sparse infrastructure make Arctic disruption by Moscow difficult to detect and expensive to repair. Underwater cables are particularly vulnerable. In September, NATO ships prevented a covert Russian operation near Svalbard involving GUGI, Russia’s specialized deep-sea directorate, and critical cable infrastructure. No damage was reported after the ships involved were confronted by NATO vessels, but the incident illustrated the potential for strategic disruption. The threat also extends onshore: arson and sabotage against ports, fuel depots, power infrastructure, and logistics hubs could disrupt civilian services and NATO reinforcement, while the use of proxy actors would further complicate attribution. GPS jamming, spoofing, and cyberattacks offer similar leverage. Russia could also adapt tactics used on NATO’s eastern flank, including drone incursions into allied airspace, to test surveillance, response times, and political resolve in the Arctic. NATO’s 2026 Resilience Baseline Requirements recognize these interconnected vulnerabilities, and coordinated electronic, cyber, and physical attacks could magnify their consequences. Research ships, fishing vessels, and commercial platforms can also provide cover for surveillance or sabotage preparations, and suspicious behavior around critical infrastructure demands scrutiny. Analysts have warned that hostile states use commercial and scientific operations as cover for threat activities in the Arctic. Svalbard in particular combines physical vulnerabilities with political pressure, and the Kremlin is using historical narratives, information operations, maritime pressure, and legal ambiguity to challenge Norwegian authority. Elsewhere, Moscow can exploit disputes over resources, environmental protection, and indigenous rights. While these concerns are legitimate, the threat lies in their deceptive manipulation and use to divide allies. Greenland presents a related challenge. Its geography, missile-warning infrastructure, and minerals make it strategically valuable, and the new US–Denmark–Greenland agreement combines an expanded American military presence with recognition of Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination. China adds another dimension. Growing Sino-Russian military and maritime cooperation in the Arctic is well documented, though their interests differ. While Moscow prioritizes control, Beijing wants access. NATO must take their cooperation seriously. Retreating sea ice has increased accessibility, but also exposure, and more traffic and infrastructure brings greater risks of accidents and confrontation. Unlike many other theaters, Arctic hybrid incidents may occur close to strategic nuclear forces, for whom a disrupted cable or satellite facility could be misread as preparation for a wider attack. For the Baltic states, this is no distant problem. North Atlantic reinforcement routes, Russia’s northern forces, and the Baltic theater form a connected strategic landscape. Defending the Baltic region and securing the High North are increasingly the same task. A stronger military posture is necessary, but troops alone cannot counter sabotage or electronic interference. NATO must detect hostile activity, withstand disruption, and impose consequences. For this task, Arctic-capable uncrewed systems can expand surveillance and improve early warning. Infrastructure protection, backup networks, and rapid repair also require cooperation with private operators and allied exercises testing simultaneous physical and cyber disruption. The decisive requirement is political, and will need to come through faster intelligence sharing, joint assessments, and pre-agreed response options. Diplomatic, economic, law-enforcement, cyber, and military instruments must give Allies choices beyond passive endurance or escalation. Uncertainty cannot become a permanent excuse for inaction. Equipment and logistics need to suit Arctic conditions, and crisis communications must help manage the risks near nuclear assets. Together, these measures should deny Moscow the expectation that hybrid aggression is cheap and safe. The Baltic, Central and Eastern European experience makes clear that recognizing hybrid aggression is not the same as deterring it. NATO’s defining Arctic test will be its response to an incident too serious to ignore, yet deliberately kept below the threshold of war. If that threshold becomes a shield against consequences, Moscow will keep exploiting it. What, then, should NATO do next? Three areas deserve a closer look without delay: satellite services and ground stations; access to critical infrastructure; and the ports, airfields, and fuel facilities on which northern reinforcement relies. They could all create opportunities for coordinated disruption during a crisis. NATO should examine where Russian probing or Chinese commercial and scientific access could expose these vulnerabilities, and whether allies could sustain operations if several vital nodes failed at once. content: 美国科技圈又出大瓜啦！ 全世界最知名的科技大佬之一，英伟达联合创始人兼CEO黄仁勋承认出轨了！ 11月8日，黄仁勋给全体员工发了一封邮件： “我欠我的家人，也欠你们所有人一个道歉。 我对我的妻子不忠，我的所作所为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我做下的事没有借口。我深感抱歉。” 整篇邮件太长，就不逐字逐句翻译了。大意就是黄仁勋向妻子、家人、英伟达的同事和合作伙伴等各方道歉，承认自己辜负了所有人的信任，也清楚道歉无法弥补错误，但会努力赢回信任云云。 众所周知，由于近些年的挖矿热和AI热，英伟达一路乘风飞起，目前已经是全球最值钱的公司之一，于是黄仁勋亲口承认婚外情的消息一传开，很快就冲上了全球各大社媒平台的热搜。 这件事让很多人大跌眼镜，因为黄仁勋这些年在外人眼里，一直是个出了名的爱妻好男人。 他和妻子洛丽（Lori）在年纪很小的时候就认识了，虽然谈不上青梅竹马，但也差不太远，俩人认识的时候才大一，黄仁勋那时甚至还没成年。 黄仁勋高中连跳了两级，考入俄勒冈州立大学时才17岁，而洛丽19岁，是他的同学。 他们学的是工科，众所周知的“少林寺”。整个实验室250个人，只有3个女生，洛丽就是其中之一。黄仁勋一眼就看上了人家，想办法跟她分到了同一个实验小组，成了她的实验搭档。 大概是上大学之前都在努力学习吧，黄仁勋追女生的方式蛮钢铁直男的——他说可以给洛丽抄作业…… “我知道自己看起来像个小孩，所以她对我的第一印象，大概就是我挺聪明的，”黄仁勋说，“我走过去问她：‘想看看我的作业吗？’然后我向她保证：‘如果你每个周日都跟我一起写作业，我保证你门门拿A。’” 他还向洛丽许诺，30岁之前要当上一家公司的CEO。这个承诺他的确实现了，只是稍微延迟了一点儿。1993年，他刚满30岁不久，就跟人合伙创办了英伟达，后来的事大家就都知道了。 后来俄勒冈州立大学曾经请黄仁勋回来演讲，他在演讲中特意提到洛丽，说认识洛丽是他大学几年里，也是他这辈子最重要的一件事。 （2009年报道原文） 两人1985年结婚，后来有了一儿一女。洛丽毕业后也当过工程师。英伟达创业的头几年，黄仁勋每周要工作80多个小时，洛丽就放弃了自己的工作，回家带孩子，家里九成的育儿工作都落在她一个人身上。 英伟达后来越做越大，黄仁勋总把这份功劳记在妻子身上： “洛丽包揽了一切，我不记得她抱怨过一次。这是她给我的礼物。” 甚至黄仁勋那身标志性的皮衣，那也是洛丽的功劳。据说黄仁勋有足足三四十件皮衣，其中大部分都是洛丽买的，因为黄仁勋自己从来不买衣服…… （黄仁勋标志性的皮衣） 总之在黄仁勋这些年的话里，英伟达走过的每一步，洛丽都参与了，公司的每一场大会、他的每一场演讲，她都在场。 直到今年，出轨的丑闻爆发前，两人在人前依然很恩爱。今年5月，黄仁勋来到中国台北，带着洛丽逛夜市，洛丽挽着他的胳膊，俩人一起吃了刨冰。 接下来就要聊到黄仁勋出轨的这位“神秘女子”了。 黄仁勋在信里没有说出对方是谁，但美国多家媒体早就报出了她的名字：英文名Alice Huang。 （Alice Huang黄仁勋） 根据目前传出来的消息，Alice Huang曾经是新加坡一家数据中心公司Megaspeed的高管。值得注意的是，这家公司是英伟达在东南亚最大的客户之一，从2024年6月到现在，一共买了超过48亿美元的英伟达芯片。 所以，双方大概率是因为工作关系认识的。出轨丑闻曝光后，各路媒体和网友猛扒以前的报道，发现两人此前就至少两次被拍到同框。讽刺的是，这两次，黄仁勋的家人都跟着他一起来了。 第一次是2024年6月，中国台北国际电脑展期间，洛丽和女儿都陪着黄仁勋来了台北。 一天晚上，技嘉科技在台北一家酒店15楼的酒吧里开派对，Alice Huang也在场。 在场的一位科技公司高管后来透露，Alice Huang当时跟大家夸下海口，说她能把黄仁勋请过来。后来黄仁勋真的来了，身边还带着两位英伟达高管。 他穿着那身黑皮衣，跟几位AI公司的高管一起喝起了威士忌。也有知情人士说，黄仁勋本来就打算去这场聚会。当晚两人的合照被一家厂商发在了自己的社交平台账号上，估计是当朋友圈发的，没想到现在成了“呈堂证供”…… 第二次是2025年5月，黄仁勋再次来到台北，这一次洛丽和孩子们也都跟来了。 5月21日晚上，他和洛丽一起在一家餐厅跟英伟达的员工吃饭。 第二天晚上，他在台北的某私厨宴请生意伙伴，Alice Huang也在席上。 黄仁勋每次来中国台湾，身边都跟着一大群记者，所以那天晚上的情形，几乎都被台湾媒体拍了下来。画面里，Alice Huang穿着一条粉色连衣裙，一直走在黄仁勋身边。 《纽约时报》甚至说台媒拍到了Alice Huang亲黄仁勋脸颊的镜头，但油管上能找到的视频没有这个画面。 （《纽时》原文说拍到了亲脸画面） 黄仁勋在餐厅门口接受记者采访的时候，Alice Huang就站在他身后。饭局结束后，两人坐同一辆车离开了。 （台湾媒体拍到的两人画面） 其实婚外情这事儿在上个月就曝光过一轮，10月29日，美国媒体最早报道两人关系密切的时候，英伟达和黄仁勋都还在否认。 英伟达对外回应说，黄仁勋和黄女士的往来“既不罕见，也不意外”。黄仁勋本人也表示，两人的往来都跟生意有关，“一切完全正常，没什么特别的”。 可事情并没有就此平息。然后11月8号，黄仁勋就向英伟达董事会承认了，随后发出了那封道歉信。从美国媒体第一次报道，到他亲口承认，前后只有10天。 这次丑闻曝光后，网上还流传出几张两人的合照，据说来自Alice Huang的朋友圈：有两人在聚会上并肩站着的，有两人在餐厅窗边举着红酒杯碰杯的，反正是真挺亲密。但据说丑闻曝光后，Alice Huang把这些照片都设成了不可见…… 对于Alice Huang此人，还有一个不得不提的部分是，不少美媒指控Alice Huang是“中国间谍”。 但对此一说，外交部已经发表了官方回应：“有关报道捕风捉影，纯属对华污蔑抹黑。” 11月9日，也就是今天，相关消息再度铺天盖地传来。 外交部发言人也再次回应：“我们此前已就此作出回应，所谓‘中国间谍’的论调纯属捕风捉影，污蔑抹黑。” （来自微博@中国新闻网） 接下来要说说下一步会如何——黄仁勋会面临什么样的结果呢？ 道歉信发出的当天，英伟达董事会已宣布对这件事展开独立调查，由独立董事组成的委员会负责，外部律师协助，黄仁勋本人不参与挑选律师。调查期间，他将继续担任CEO。 按英伟达自己的规矩，这件事并不是小事。英伟达的员工行为准则里，明确将“个人关系”列为可能造成利益冲突的情形，要求当事人回避相关决策，违反准则的人可能受到处分，最严重的后果就是开除。 有媒体认为，按以往的惯例，美国公司的CEO一旦被曝出婚外情，董事会往往几天之内就会让他走人。 但这种惯例在英伟达是否成立呢？难说。 简单来说就是，英伟达内部没有一个明显可以接黄仁勋班的人。黄仁勋管公司从来不讲传统的层级，60多个高管都直接向他汇报，公司所有的大事最后都由他一个人拍板。 他还持有英伟达3.56％的股份，是公司最大的个人股东。董事会除他之外的10个人里，其中4人是在90年代就跟他一起打天下的老相识，所以很难说他会面临什么后果。 根据三位前员工的说法，黄仁勋一直把董事会看作“满足公司治理要求的摆设”，从来没指望董事会在经营上起什么作用。这几年，他还把儿子、女儿和女婿都安排进了英伟达，三个人在公司里的权力越来越大，公司内部有人对此不满，也有人觉得他是在培养儿女接班。 但无论如何，英伟达的股价是保不住了，今天周一盘前就暴跌了5%…… 根据《卫报》的估算，这让整个英伟达的市值瞬间蒸发了3000亿美元。 （英伟达市值蒸发3000亿） 至于黄仁勋本人，这事可以说才刚刚开始。 11月17日，英伟达就要公布最新一季的财报，到时候这件事肯定躲不过去。 最近亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人会议又要在深圳开幕，美国总统特朗普曾说会带上黄仁勋一起去。这事儿一出，不知道他还会不会来…… 篇幅有限，咱们先吃到这儿。现在看社交媒体上，各路媒体和网友还在发力，估计可能还会扒出更多，咱们到时候继续~ title: Huawei says it’s made a 100 percent Chinese PC
zh_title: 华为称其生产的 PC 100% 中国制造
summary: 华为声称其生产的台式电脑仅使用中国制造的零部件。该公司上周推出了青云HM650，并表示其采用华为自家的麒麟X90处理器，是一款十核20线程的机器，主频为2.3GHz。该机器运行新开发的企业版HarmonyOS，华为开发该操作系统是为了结束对Android的依赖，并打算在其生产的大多数设备上运行该操作系统。据报道，一个中国政府机构已签约购买 600 台机器。这并不表明这台机器是一种好奇心，因为北京已经命令所有政府
content:
华为声称其生产的台式电脑仅使用中国制造的零部件。该公司上周推出了青云HM650，并表示其采用华为自家的麒麟X90处理器，是一款十核20线程的机器，主频为2.3GHz。该机器运行新开发的企业版HarmonyOS，华为开发该操作系统是为了结束对Android的依赖，并打算在其生产的大多数设备上运行该操作系统。据报道，一个中国政府机构已签约购买 600 台机器。这并不表明这台机器是一种新奇的东西，因为北京已下令所有政府实体从 Wintel 盒子转向本地替代品。据报道，虽然华为声称该机的零部件 100% 是由本土公司制造，但目前尚不清楚所有这些零部件是否都采用中国设计。 《登记册》提到了这种不确定性，因为许多非中国公司继续在中国经营工厂。即使华为使用的一些部件不完全是中国的，青云HM650的亮相对于英特尔、AMD和高通来说也是个坏消息，因为内存成本上涨导致PC市场萎缩，这三家公司都在遭受损失。中国政府是一个巨大的买家，失去竞购其业务的机会不太可能有帮助。日本在网络攻击浪潮后宣布紧急应对计划 日本政府上周五宣布提供紧急资金，帮助当地组织加强国家网络防御。
这一价值 100 亿日元（约合 6300 万美元）的救助计划是在一波网络攻击浪潮袭来之后推出的，这些攻击已经对铁路、零售商、肯德基物流提供商和云计算运营商造成了干扰。该紧急救助计划旨在帮助日本政府机构利用人工智能来掌握信息安全基础知识，并构建工具让国家网络安全办公室汇总有关网络攻击的信息。一些资金也将用于支持受害者。联想亚太区负责人调任摩托罗拉负责人继将负责人阿马尔·巴布(Amar Babu)调任摩托罗拉移动业务集团总经理兼全球总裁后，联想正在寻找亚太区业务的新领导者。阿马尔在该地区领导联想超过五年，该公司称赞他将联想转变为“更加平衡和多元化的业务以及关键的增长引擎”。公司公告称：“在整个产品组合中，AP 保持了第一大个人电脑的地位，而我们的移动业务则实现了显着增长，摩托罗拉在印度的市场份额达到近 9%，在日本成为第二大智能手机 OEM 厂商。” “我们的基础设施业务实现了盈利增长，市场份额接近两位数，而解决方案和服务继续巩固其最佳行业地位，并将其先进服务业务组合大幅增加至 50% 以上。”联想尚未为其亚太地区前哨基地任命新的领导者。
越南赞扬国产 USB 存储芯片 越南政府上周宣布推出该国首款国产安全芯片 - 一款 28 纳米设备，显然在硅中集成了加密算法。该芯片已用于安全 USB 存储设备，越南政府使用这些设备为政府和国防机构以及共产党存储信息。该国希望使用这些芯片来确保国家数字签名认证系统以及电力、水、石油和天然气以及电信等关键基础设施系统的安全存储。河内表示，该芯片在发布之前需要进行更多测试

Huawei claims it’s built a desktop PC that uses only parts made in CHina. The company launched the Qingyun HM650 last week and said it uses Huawei’s own Kirin X90 processor, a ten-core 20-thread machine with a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The machine runs a newly developed enterprise version of HarmonyOS, the OS Huawei developed to end its dependence on Android and which it intends to run on most of the devices it makes. A single Chinese government agency has reportedly signed up for 600 of the machines. That’s not an indication this machine is a curiosity, because Beijing has ordered all government entities to shift from Wintel boxes to local alternatives. While Huawei has reportedly claimed local companies manufactured 100 percent of the components in the machine, it is unclear if all those components use Chinese designs. The Register mentions that uncertainty as many non-Chinese companies continue to operate factories in China. Even if Huawei is using some parts that aren’t entirely Chinese, the debut of the Qingyun HM650 is bad news for Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm, as all are suffering as the PC market shrinks due to the rising cost of memory. China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful. Japan announces emergency response package after wave of cyberattacks Japan’s government last Friday announced emergency funding to help local organizations strengthen the nation's cyber-defences. The ¥10 billion ($63 million) package follows a wave of cyberattacks that have disrupted railways, retailers, KFC’s logistics provider , and cloud computing operators . The emergency package aims to help Japanese government agencies to use AI to nail infosec basics, and to build tools that let the National Cybersecurity Office aggregate information about cyberattacks. Some funds will also go towards supporting victims. Lenovo’s APAC boss shifts to lead Motorola Lenovo is looking for a new leader of its Asia-Pacific operations after shifting the boss, Amar Babu, to a role as mobile business group general manager and global president at Motorola. Amar led Lenovo in the region for over five years and the company credited him with turning it into “a more balanced and diversified business and a key growth engine.” “Across the portfolio, AP maintained its #1 PC position, while our mobile business achieved notable growth, with Motorola reaching nearly 9 percent market share in India and the #2 smartphone OEM in Japan,” according to a company announcement . “Our infrastructure business achieved profitable growth and nearly double-digit market share, while Solutions & Services continued to strengthen its best-of-breed industry position and significantly increased its advanced services business mix to over 50 percent.” Lenovo has not named a new leader for its APAC outpost. Vietnam hails homegrown USB storage chip Vietnam’s government last week announced the nation’s first domestically-designed security chip - a 28-nanometer device that apparently integrates encryption algorithms in silicon. The chip is already in use on secure USB storage devices that Vietnam’s government employs to store info for government and defense agencies, plus the Communist Party. The nation hopes to use the chips to secure storage of the national digital signature certification system, and critical infrastructure systems in electricity, water, oil and gas, and telecommunications. Hanoi says the chip needs more testing before the government will trust it to protect state secrets, but hailed the chip as an important step towards development of sovereign security capabilities. Apple’s biggest ever education deal Apple last week quietly announced it has won its biggest-ever sale of Macs into the education market in the Philippines. Speaking on the company’s Q4 earnings call, CEO John Ternus said Apple sold 172,000 MacBook Neos to the Department of Education in the Philippines, which will deploy them to teachers and staff. ®

title: Former NATO Commander: Putin Wants China to Take Asia, Russia to Take Europe and America to Stay Home
zh_title: 北约前司令：普京希望中国占领亚洲，俄罗斯占领欧洲和美国留在国内
summary: 第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 5 日在白宫会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的特使基里尔·德米特里耶夫。白宫官方视频截图。前北约欧洲盟军最高司令、退休将军菲利普·布里德洛夫 (Philip Breedlove) 11 月 8 日警告称，普京打算将世界划分为三个势力范围。根据该计划，“中国控制远东，俄罗斯控制欧洲，美国控制西半球，”布里德洛夫告诉福克斯新闻数字频道。几天前，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示与莫斯科即将达成的协议可能会达成一致。
content:
第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普于 2026 年 11 月 5 日在白宫会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的特使基里尔·德米特里耶夫。白宫官方视频截图。前北约欧洲盟军最高司令、退休将军菲利普·布里德洛夫 (Philip Breedlove) 11 月 8 日警告称，普京打算将世界划分为三个势力范围。根据该计划，“中国控制远东，俄罗斯控制欧洲，美国控制西半球，”布里德洛夫告诉福克斯新闻数字频道。他发出警告的几天前，唐纳德·特朗普总统表示即将与莫斯科达成的协议可能会延伸到乌克兰以外的地区，而距离美国、乌克兰和俄罗斯谈判代表在阿布扎比举行会议还有两天。 11 月 5 日在白宫会见普京特使基里尔·德米特里耶夫后，特朗普承诺达成一项“伟大而美好的协议”，该协议“将不仅仅涉及乌克兰”，而且“可能涉及整个欧洲”。 11 月 8 日，他表示乌克兰将在这一过程中出现“一点点不同的面貌”。欧洲领导人拒绝任何在没有他们参与的情况下重塑欧洲大陆安全的美俄协议。乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基告诉美国有线电视新闻网，这样的安排将是复杂的，并且有潜在的危险。 11月10日至11日举行的阿布扎比​​会谈将是自2月份日内瓦会谈以来的首场三方会谈。特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳将率领美国代表团。
俄罗斯将派出总统助理弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基、外交部副部长谢尔盖·里亚布科夫和米哈伊尔·加鲁津以及总参谋部官员。法国外长让-诺尔·巴罗表示欧洲将派代表出席，但克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示，俄罗斯只与美国人举行安全会谈，没有与欧洲人举行安全会谈。布里德洛夫表示，普京“已多次向领导人推行该计划”，并补充道，“他谈论过这个计划，也写过这个计划。”布里德洛夫警告说，如果俄罗斯的最高要求保持不变，而欧洲必须牺牲安全来实现和平，“这不会顺利。”他说普京“从来都不是乌克兰的和平伙伴”，而且“普京先生正在与西方交战”。俄罗斯在全面入侵前两个月以书面形式提出了要求。 2021年12月17日，其外交部公布了北约-俄罗斯协议草案和美俄条约草案。北约草案要求不再扩大联盟规模，并禁止北约在乌克兰、东欧、高加索和中亚地区进行军事活动。美国的草案要求两国移除驻扎在其境外的核武器，这将迫使美国从欧洲撤出核武器。普京对俄罗斯失去领土的看法早在战争之前就已存在。根据克里姆林宫的英文文本，他在 2005 年向联邦议会发表的讲话中称苏联的解体是“本世纪的一场重大地缘政治灾难”。
当他于 2022 年 2 月 24 日宣布入侵乌克兰时，他将“北约向东扩张”视为“对我们国家生存的威胁”。 2023年3月31日，普京批准了俄罗斯现行的外交政策构想，该构想将俄罗斯描述为独特的“国家文明”和“俄罗斯世界”的中心。美国和平研究所称该文件是对现行国际秩序和美国在其中的领导作用的否定。莫斯科长期以来一直声称西方承诺不会扩大北约，但没有任何条约禁止该联盟接纳新成员。 1990 年德国条约

【原文 English Original】
First Lady Melania Trump meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s special envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, at the White House on November 5, 2026. Screenshot from official White House video. Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, warned on Nov. 8 that Putin intends to divide the world into three spheres of influence. Under that plan, “China controls the Far East, Russia controls Europe, and America controls the Western Hemisphere,” Breedlove told Fox News Digital . His warning came days after President Donald Trump said a coming deal with Moscow could reach beyond Ukraine , and two days before U.S., Ukrainian and Russian negotiators meet in Abu Dhabi. After meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House on Nov. 5, Trump promised a “big, beautiful agreement” that was “going to involve more than Ukraine” and “might involve all of Europe.” On Nov. 8, he said Ukraine would emerge from the process “a little bit different shape.” European leaders rejected any U.S.-Russian deal that reshapes the continent’s security without their involvement . Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told CNN that such an arrangement would be complicated and potentially dangerous . The Abu Dhabi talks on Nov. 10 and 11 will be the first three-way round since Geneva in February . Special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will lead the U.S. delegation. Russia is sending presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, and General Staff officers . French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Europe will be represented, but Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia has held security talks only with the Americans and none with Europeans . Breedlove said Putin “has pushed that plan on leaders several times,” adding, “He talks about it, and he writes about it.” If Russia’s maximalist demands remain intact and Europe must sacrifice its security to achieve peace, Breedlove warned, “this is not going to go well.” He said Putin “has never been a partner for peace in Ukraine” and that “Mr. Putin is at war” with the West. Russia set out its demands in writing two months before the full-scale invasion. On Dec. 17, 2021, its Foreign Ministry published a draft NATO-Russia agreement and a draft U.S.-Russia treaty . The NATO draft demanded no further enlargement of the alliance and a ban on NATO military activity in Ukraine, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus, and Central Asia . The U.S. draft required both countries to remove nuclear weapons stationed outside their territory , which would have forced the withdrawal of American nuclear weapons from Europe. Putin’s view of Russia’s lost territory predates the war. In his 2005 address to the Federal Assembly, he called the Soviet Union’s collapse “a major geopolitical disaster of the century,” according to the Kremlin’s English text . When he announced the invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, he cited “the expansion of NATO to the east” as a threat “to the very existence of our state.” On March 31, 2023, Putin approved Russia’s current Foreign Policy Concept , which describes the country as a distinct “state-civilization” and the center of “the Russian world.” The U.S. Institute of Peace called the document a repudiation of the current international order and America’s leading role in it. Moscow has long claimed the West promised not to enlarge NATO, but no treaty bars the alliance from admitting new members. The 1990 treaty on German reunification restricted NATO forces in East Germany only . Secretary of State James Baker’s remark that year to Gorbachev that NATO would not move “1 inch to the east” referred to East Germany during the reunification talks. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, signed by Russia, states that it will not “limit or dilute” NATO’s opening to new members. Belarus already serves as a Russian forward base. Russia deployed its nuclear-capable Oreshnik missile there in December 2025. Belarus puts its range at up to 5,000 km, enough to reach most of Europe. Russia had previously stationed tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, and its 2024 nuclear doctrine placed the country under Russia’s nuclear umbrella. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said in November 2025 that German intelligence warned Russia is creating the option of war against NATO by 2029 at the latest, an assessment Breedlove endorsed at the time. In June, German Army chief Lt. Gen. Christian Freuding called that timeline “NATO-agreed intelligence” , saying all 32 allies agree Russia could be capable of invading a NATO country that year. German Chief of Defense Gen. Carsten Breuer warned an attack could come earlier , while Estonian intelligence assesses that Russia will not attack a NATO member this year or next. Russia’s ability to keep fighting depends on its economy, which has proved more resilient than early forecasts suggested. In 2022, the International Monetary Fund predicted it would shrink 8.5% . It contracted by about 1.2%, then grew in 2023 and 2024. Russia’s economy is projected to reach $2.86 trillion this year, making it the eighth largest in the world. The Soviet Union sustained a 10-year war in Afghanistan and a four-decade military rivalry with the United States; its economy measured $791 billion in nominal dollars in 1990. Anyone expecting economic pressure to force Moscow to end the war is likely to wait a long time. Sanctions have slowed Russia’s economy without cutting off its income. Growth is forecast at about 1% this year , and the budget is in deficit for a fifth consecutive year. Yet Russian fossil fuel exports earned about €625 million a day in September. China was the largest buyer, while sanctioned shadow-fleet tankers carried 57% of Russia’s seaborne oil. The European Union still bought €1.7 billion of Russian energy that month, mostly natural gas. Ukraine cannot match that export income in a war of endurance. At September’s rate, Russia’s annual fossil fuel earnings would total about €228 billion, more than five times the roughly $40 billion Ukraine earns from all its goods exports combined. Ukrainian agricultural exports brought in $22.5 billion in 2025, down from a record $27.9 billion in 2021. Russia also has a much larger pool of potential soldiers, with about five times Ukraine’s population. Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service estimates Russia’s mobilization resource at 25 million people , about 3 million of them trained. In 2023, Moscow added older men to that pool, raising the age to which rank-and-file reservists can be mobilized to 55, and junior officers to 60 , phased in through 2028. Government-controlled Ukraine has about 28.5 million people , and more than 4.4 million Ukrainians, about 11% of the pre-war population, now live in the EU under temporary protection. Ukraine is drawing soldiers from a population that continues to shrink. If Ukraine runs short of soldiers, Europe is unlikely to supply them. A poll covering all NATO members in September and October 2025 found that 27% of Germans , 25% of Italians and 30% of the Dutch said they would fight for their own country, compared with 49% of Poles. Presumably, even fewer would be willing to fight for Ukraine. The post Former NATO Commander: Putin Wants China to Take Asia, Russia to Take Europe and America to Stay Home appeared first on The Gateway Pundit .

title: 台湾人民共产党主席林德旺因涉嫌接受中共指示和资助参选里长遭羁押
summary: 资料照片：在台湾台北举行“台美国防产业论坛”期间，台湾人民共产党主席林德旺(中)在台北国际会议中心外参加抗议活动。(2023年5月3日) 台湾当局星期天(11月8日)表示，已以接受中国共产党指示和资助参选台湾基层选举的罪嫌，羁押台湾人民共产党主席林德旺。另一名接受林德旺安排参选台湾基层选举的该党中央委员陈震宙则交保候审。 台湾台南地方检察署星期天发布新闻稿称，台南地检署和新竹地检署不久前分别接获境外势力介入台湾即将举行的地方选举的情资，遂组成专案小组共同侦办。 检方专案小组一
content:
资料照片：在台湾台北举行“台美国防产业论坛”期间，台湾人民共产党主席林德旺(中)在台北国际会议中心外参加抗议活动。(2023年5月3日)
台湾当局星期天(11月8日)表示，已以接受中国共产党指示和资助参选台湾基层选举的罪嫌，羁押台湾人民共产党主席林德旺。另一名接受林德旺安排参选台湾基层选举的该党中央委员陈震宙则交保候审。
台湾台南地方检察署星期天发布新闻稿称，台南地检署和新竹地检署不久前分别接获境外势力介入台湾即将举行的地方选举的情资，遂组成专案小组共同侦办。
检方专案小组一共传唤了14名被告及9名证人。经讯问和初步调查，检方高度怀疑林德旺和陈震宙涉嫌犯罪，并担心两人可能潜逃或销毁证据，因此分别向当地法院申请将两人羁押禁见。
根据台湾中央社的报道，法院裁准了检方对林德旺的羁押申请，而陈震宙则获准以5万元新台币(约合1525美元)交保候审。报道还说，其余被传唤的被告在调查过程中已陆续获释。
台湾将于11月28日举行新一轮被称为“九合一”的地方公职人员选举，一共要选出9类地方公职人员，包括6个直辖市长、16个县市长在内的共81位县市长候选人，以及县市议员、乡镇市长、里长，应选总名额达11051人。
台湾总统赖清德并不在此次选举的选票上，但是选举却被视为选民对赖清德施政的“期中考”，有些类似于美国刚刚结束的“中期选举”。九合一选举通常也被视为2028年台湾总统大选的一场“前哨战”。
根据台南地检署发布的新闻稿，初步调查发现，林德旺不仅接受中共的指示和资助，亲自参选台南市新营区太南里里长选举，而且还安排陈震宙参选新竹市北区武陵里里长选举。
里长是台湾行政区划中最基层的官员，位阶不高，权力也不大，但是却能和最基层的选民密切交往互动，在台湾总统大选或其他重要的选举中有可能影响基层选民的投票意向。
过去在台湾总统大选或其他重要的选举中，当局经常指控台海对岸的中国政府非法干预台湾的选举，通过与其关系密切的台湾人士组织包括里长在内的台湾基层官员前往中国大陆接受招待旅游，为特定的政党和候选人造势和拉票。
此次检方就还指控林德旺试图通过多次招募选民前往中国大陆并接受招待的方式进行“买票”即贿选。
台湾是个民主社会，因此林德旺任主席的台湾人民共产党得以依法在台湾注册与活动。林德旺与该党成员也经常在台北的街头举行游行或抗议示威活动。不过，林德旺和他领导的共产党在台湾并没有多大市场，也没有多少影响力。
这并非他首次因涉嫌与中国大陆的关联而陷入法律纠纷。林德旺此前曾与该党另一名领导人一同被控涉及“中国渗透”及企图干预选举，但最终在2025年被判无罪。
经常会对台湾事务评头论足的中国国务院台湾事务办公室截至本文发稿，尚未对林德旺被羁押和陈震宙交保一事发表公开评论，但它常常抨击赖清德政府奉行所谓“台独”分裂的政策。北京还称赖清德为“顽固的台独分子”，并拒绝他多次提出的在不预设前提的基础上进行对等、有尊严两岸对话的建议。
台海两岸同文同种，但是自1949年起便分离分治、互不隶属。北京当局坚称拥有对台湾的主权，而且即使诉诸武力，也要实现两岸的统一。多届中国政府多年来除了以各种方式干预和影响台湾政治和选举外，还一直在建军备战，终极目标就是实现所谓“两岸统一”。
台湾的民进党政府拒绝北京对台湾的主权诉求，并坚持认为，中华民国早已是一个主权独立的国家，而台湾的未来只能由其2300万人民自行决定。
近年来，两岸关系持续紧张。中国政府持续对台文攻武吓，同过出动机舰常态化在台湾周边海空域举行军事演习或战备警巡向台湾施加强大的军事压力。中国军方的舰艇、海警船和民兵船最近甚至出入台湾东部海域，向台湾示威。

content:
最新数据显示，10月中国工业生产者出厂价格指数（PPI）创近四年半以来最快增速。图为新疆和田地区的一个生产车间内，工人在缝制企业定制的工作服装。 （新华社）
中东冲突推高能源成本，带动10月中国工业生产者出厂价格指数（PPI）创近四年半以来最快增速。家庭需求疲软，则使得同期居民消费价格指数（CPI）涨幅回落。
受访学者认为，10月通胀数据显示中国供需仍不平衡，需求端没有得到明显改善。
中国国家统计局星期一（11月9日）发布数据显示，10月PPI同比上涨5.7%，高于9月份5.0%的涨幅，也高于路透社和彭博社调查预测的5.3%。
国家统计局城市司首席统计师董莉娟解读，煤炭开采和洗选业、石油和天然气开采，以及计算机通信和其他电子设备制造业等九个行业，合计拉动PPI同比上涨约6.14个百分点。
另一方面，10月CPI同比上涨0.7%，涨幅较9月回落0.2个百分点；食品价格同比降幅从上月的1.7%扩大至2.9%，成为影响CPI涨幅的主要因素。
其中，鲜菜、肉类、蛋类以及鲜果价格合计影响CPI同比下降约0.54个百分点。消费品、黄金首饰以及服务在内的其他类别价格涨幅也均有所放缓。
剔除波动较大的食品和能源价格，核心CPI同比涨幅从9月份的1.0%降至10月的0.8%，与今年低点持平。
新加坡国立大学东亚研究所高级研究员陈波向《联合早报》分析，10月数据反映中国国内供需仍不平衡，消费品价格虽有上升，但幅度较预期要小，“消费需求没有得到明显改善”。
经济学人智库高级经济学家徐天辰受访时说，中东局势再度紧张引发全球油价上涨，是上个月PPI上涨的主要驱动因素，但食品价格回落对冲了能源通胀。
尽管国际能源紧张和全球人工智能（AI）热潮推高石油及金属等大宗商品价格，导致整体出厂价格飙升。但由于家庭需求疲弱限制了消费支出，上游价格压力尚未完全传导到消费端。
花旗集团经济师警告称，中国短期内存在“恶性通胀”风险，即由大宗商品成本驱动的价格上涨。
花旗报告指出，尽管围绕油价和中东局势的不确定性升高，但短期内PPI仍面临上行风险，CPI则面对下行风险。“能源价格仍取决于全球市场行情，如果油价回归常态，通缩风险可能卷土重来。”
中国国家发展改革委主任郑栅洁上个月在一场民营企业座谈会上表示，要正视“外部冲击，供强需弱”等现实难题。
陈波说，中国自身能源供给的韧性非常有潜力，但能源危机造成的价格上涨，还是会波及到生产者。随着时间进入冬季，能源价格或将维持相对高位，“企业成本方面的压力可能还是存在”。
徐天辰则认为，明年PPI回落的可能性偏高。他说：“一方面是油价易降难升，另一方面是（中国）国内需求比较温和，对通胀的推力有限。”

summary: 台湾尚未选出新驻马绍尔群岛特使：外交部 - 焦点台湾 台湾尚未选出新驻马绍尔群岛特使：外交部 要启动文字转语音服务，请先同意以下隐私政策。中新社台北11月9日电 台湾外交部周一表示，在前任驻马绍尔群岛大使因国庆变装秀引发争议而离职后，台湾仍在遴选新任驻马绍尔群岛大使。徐蔚民上月底在排练完演出后被勒令辞去大使职务。
content:
外交部：台湾尚未选出新驻马绍尔群岛特使 - 聚焦台湾
外交部：台湾尚未选出新驻马绍尔群岛特使
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月9日电 台湾外交部周一表示，在前任驻马绍尔群岛大使因国庆变装秀引发争议而离职后，台湾仍在遴选新任驻马绍尔群岛大使。
徐蔚民为10月10日国庆庆典排练演出被外交部认定为“不当”，上月底被勒令辞去大使职务。
周一被问及是否已选出新大使时，外交部告诉中央社，“考虑到台湾驻外外交使节肩负的重大责任”，遴选过程仍在进行中。
外交部补充说：“外交部将综合考虑国家总体外交政策、运作要求、专业能力和个人诚信，尽快挑选合适的人选任命。”
与此同时，中华民国驻马绍尔群岛大使馆由副馆长刘汉清公使领导，运作正常。
外交部发表此番言论之前，当地媒体周一早些时候报道称，内阁最近批准了外交部将徐召回台北的建议，并从 11 月 5 日起将他调往外交部外交国际事务研究所。
在一段马绍尔群岛国庆变装表演活动排练视频曝光后，徐面临两党的批评，视频显示，作为表演的一部分，他坐在小木床上，由八名马绍尔男子作为担架抬着。
外交部长林佳龙在10月28日的立法院听证会上表示，外交部已召回徐，以解释情况，并确保今后不再发生类似事件。
林补充说，徐事件不会影响台湾与马绍尔群岛之间的外交关系。
许是近几个月来第二位因争议而被召回台北的台湾外交官。
台湾驻日内瓦代表处负责人李冠德上月底被免职，原因是他的同事投诉职场欺凌行为，调查小组后来证实了这一点。
此外，李在七月下旬还被指控滥用公共资源谋取个人目的。外交部告诉中央社，这些指控仍在调查中。
李被召回台湾后，一直在台北外交部总部工作。
外交部非政府组织国际司副司长康嘉棋已被任命为继任者。

Taiwan yet to select new envoy to Marshall Islands: MOFA
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 9 (CNA) Taiwan is still in the process of selecting a new ambassador to the Marshall Islands, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said Monday, following the departure of the previous envoy amid a controversy over a proposed drag show on National Day.
Herbert Hsu (徐蔚民) was ordered to leave his ambassadorial post late last month after his rehearsal of the show for the Oct. 10 Taiwan National Day celebrations was deemed "inappropriate" by MOFA.
Asked on Monday whether a new ambassador had been chosen, MOFA told CNA that the selection process was still ongoing, "given the significant responsibilities entrusted to Taiwan's diplomatic envoys abroad."
"The ministry will take into account the nation's overall foreign policy, operational requirements, professional competence, and personal integrity before picking a suitable candidate for appointment as soon as possible," MOFA added.
In the meantime, the Republic of China (Taiwan) Embassy in the Marshall Islands is being headed by its second-in-command, Minister Hank Liu (劉漢清), and its operations are continuing normally, MOFA said.
MOFA's comments came after local media reported earlier Monday that the Cabinet had recently approved the ministry's recommendation to recall Hsu to Taipei, and that he had been reassigned to MOFA's Institute of Diplomacy and International Affairs, with effect from Nov. 5.
Hsu faced bipartisan criticism after a video of a rehearsal for a National Day drag show event in the Marshall Islands emerged, showing him sitting on small wooden bed being carried as a litter by eight Marshallese men, as part of the performance.
During a legislative hearing on Oct. 28, Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) said the ministry had recalled Hsu to explain the circumstances and to ensure that there would be no similar incidents in the future.
The Hsu incident would not affect diplomatic ties between Taiwan and the Marshall Islands, Lin added.
Hsu was the second Taiwanese diplomat to be recalled to Taipei in recent months due to controversy.
Greg Lee (李冠德), who headed Taiwan's representative office in Geneva, was removed from his post in the Swiss city late last month, following complaints by his colleagues of workplace bullying, which an investigative team later confirmed.
In addition, Lee was also accused in late July of misusing public resources for personal purposes. MOFA told CNA that those accusations were still under investigation.
Since his recall to Taiwan, Lee has been working at MOFA's headquarters in Taipei.
Kang Chia-chi (康嘉棋), deputy head of MOFA's Department of NGO International Affairs, has been named his successor.

# 网路袭击法国境内超市冷藏设备是伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队干的， 法国外长发誓要制裁

法国 –  法国周一表示，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队是上个月针对法国境内超市冷藏设备所发动“史无前例”网络攻击的幕后黑手，并誓言将在欧洲层面针对德黑兰实施制裁。

继续浏览后续

10月11日至12日发生的网络攻击波及了法国多家超市，导致冷藏设备温度升高，部分超市被迫丢弃了库存中所有易腐食品。

法国外交部长巴罗在谈到这次网络攻击时表示：“我可以确认，这次攻击是由伊朗伊斯兰共和国的伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）所为。”

他在巴黎出席七国集团（G7）外长会议期间表示：“这次攻击在规模和攻击强度上都是史无前例的。”

巴黎检察官在另一份声明中表示，已针对“沙希德·卡维”， 即伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队旗下的一支隐秘网络部队——展开调查。

巴罗仅明确提到了针对法国连锁超市系统的攻击，据他称，共有700个网点受到波及。法国外长说：“我们将在欧洲层面，对所有相关责任方实施制裁。”

欧洲其他国家也报告了类似的事件。

法新社报道，11月2日，至少另外九个欧洲国家的各类食品杂货店遭遇了疑似针对其冷冻系统的网络攻击。

正值欧洲各国持续支持乌克兰对抗俄罗斯之际，官方曾发出警告，说存在来自俄罗斯的网络攻击风险；而此次事件无疑在欧洲引发了震动。

近几天，欧洲的空中交通也受到干扰，数十个航班收到虚假炸弹威胁，尽管这些威胁的来源还不明确。

美国和以色列与伊朗之间爆发了一场战争，这场战争始于2月28日伊朗最高领袖阿里·哈梅内伊被杀事件。

欧洲国家并没有卷入这场冲突，但法国官员指责伊朗散布虚假信息，涉及过去一个月里席卷法国的抗议活动。

content:
中国近年来加大了对地下家庭教会的打压（资料图片）图像来源: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/picture alliance
（德国之声中文网）崔献峰（圣名周子逊）创办了北京佳全教会。其妻子、韩国籍基督徒崔进荣（Jin Young Gu）表示，崔献峰于10月23日被捕，罪名是诈骗。
崔进荣说，崔献峰此前已于9月4日被拘留。当时，约有100名警察突袭了教会。
她表示，所谓诈骗指控与教会成员的奉献款有关。她认为，这类指控很可能与教会未经注册有关。
美联社就此向北京市石景山区警方寻求置评，但未获回应。中国外交部尚未回应美联社发出的相关询问。
此次逮捕是中国国家主席习近平长期以来加强宗教管控行动的最新案例之一。中国当局一直致力于强化对宗教团体的管控，以确保所有宗教组织都遵守中国共产党领导。
金明日在美国总统特朗普出面之后获准离境前往美国（图为2018年资料照片）图像来源: Ng Han Guan/AP Photo/picture alliance
2025年10月，中国当局展开了近年来规模最大的宗教活动打压行动之一，在多个城市连夜突击搜查后，逮捕了锡安教会30名负责人。锡安教会是中国最大规模地下基督教会。
被捕者包括教会创办人金明日。今年7月，在美国总统特朗普访华期间亲自向习近平提出请求后，金明日获释。
崔进荣表示，北京佳全教会成立于2006年。作为一个未经注册的教会团体，其规模此后不断扩大。在过去二十年间，该教会曾多次面临当局的干扰，敬拜场所数度遭封锁。
她说，2019年，当局封闭了该教会在北京的聚会场所，迫使信徒改以小组形式，并在不同地点进行小规模聚会。
崔进荣还表示，2023年，当局曾中断一次周日教会课程，并警告她和崔献峰，称教会规模已经过大。
“他们告诉他，只能带领一个人数少于100人的教会。”崔进荣说，“这是当局针对我们教会的规模和组织方式发出的直接警告。”
崔进荣是韩国公民。她表示，自2023年以来，当局一直拒绝向她发放签证，使她无法以家庭成员身份返回中国。

被拘押近九个月的中国家庭教会领袖金明日在美国独立日当天获释，已经抵达美国。其家人与人权组织感谢特朗普为其获释做出的努力，但提醒仍有多名锡安教会成员被关押。

content:
Skip to news navigation, settings and search
Posted Fri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pmFri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pmFri 6 Nov 2026 at 1:50pm
去年中国灵活就业人员数量已超过2亿人。 (AP:Andy Wong)
与许多中国零工经济从业者一样，自由摄影师阿梅（Ah May）未来退休可能无法依靠养老金。
她经常四处跑，收入并不稳定，负担不起全部费用每月千元人民币（约213澳元）的中国“社会保险”。
“对我来说有一点贵了。我目前收入不高，没有办法交上，”阿梅说。出于隐私考虑，她要求媒体仅使用她的英文名字。
中国面向城镇劳动者的社会保障网络采用保险制模式，要求参保人或其雇主持续缴费。
该体系包括医疗、养老、失业、工伤和生育保险等组成部分。
雇主为员工缴纳社保是法定义务，而个体经营者则可自愿选择是否参保。
今年10月，时任人力资源和社会保障部副部长李忠表示，政府将利用大数据识别未参保人员。
他说，目标是建立一个“更加优化更可持续”的社会保障网，并使其“更密、更牢靠”。
自11月1日起，对于未依法缴纳社保的雇主，处罚标准也已统一，最高可处以应缴保险费用三倍的罚款。
经济学家认为，将社会保障网络覆盖至更多人群，可以使民众减少应急储蓄，从而提振家庭消费支出。
阿梅目前只缴纳医保部分，每月需支付数百元，这已经占了她月收入中的很大一部分。她认为，如果完全自费承担医疗开支，成本会更高。
她表示，自己也希望拥有养老保险保障，但看不到能够负担得起的办法。
“除非有一些福利补贴的政策[缴纳完整保险费用]。”她说。
不少人表示，自己承担不起全部社保费用。 (AP: Mark Schiefelbein)
根据全国人大2025年12月发布的一份报告，中国有超过2亿人从事灵活就业。
这一群体包括自由职业者，以及通过各类应用程序和网站提供劳务、服务或商品的个体平台劳动者。
官方媒体《中国青年报》今年早些时候发布的一项针对1400名平台劳动者的调查显示，在35岁以下受访者中，77%表示愿意自行缴费参加社会保险。
一些年轻人表示，退休年龄提高，使他们对缴纳养老保险是否划算产生了疑虑。 (Reuters: Tingshu Wang)
然而，该调查还发现，真正足额缴纳社保的年轻平台劳动者仅约占17%。
一些灵活就业人员和个体经营者由于无法确定30年后的情况，在20多岁或30多岁时选择不缴纳养老保险。
独立从事金融产品交易的李先生（Lucian Li）便是其中之一。
“自己做交易这么多年，我觉得这个收益率远远超社保。”
悉尼新南威尔士大学（UNSW Sydney）社会政策教授李秉勤表示，政府这些年来一直在逐步加强对未依法缴纳社保费企业的执法力度。
2025年，中国最高法院裁定，企业与员工之间为了节约成本而放弃缴纳社保的私下协议无效。
然而，李教授指出，对企业处以罚款以及让更多人加入社保体系，并不能解决中国社会保障制度面临的根本挑战。
中国人口老龄化意味着缴纳养老金的劳动年龄人口不断减少，而领取养老金的老年人口持续增加。
根据中国国家统计局数据，中国60岁及以上人口已达3.23亿，占总人口约23%。
预计到2030年，这一数字将增至约3.9亿，而劳动年龄人口则将进一步缩减。
李教授表示，中国学者早在2019年就曾提出，对企业职工养老基金而言，到2028年前后可能开始出现收不抵支，并在2035年前后耗尽结余。
“后续更新研究认为，延迟退休政策可能将这一时间点推迟8至9年，”她说。
自2025年起，中国政府开始在15年期限内逐步提高法定退休年龄：蓝领女性由50岁提高至55岁，白领女性由55岁提高至58岁，男性则由60岁提高至63岁。
“[中国社保体系]短期内不存在支付危机，但确实面临现实的结构性[人口]压力。”她说。

title: Amnesia? Witness ‘evasive’ response draws ire of senator-judges
zh_title: 健忘症？证人“回避”回应引起参议员法官的愤怒
summary: 副总统萨拉·杜特尔特 (Sara Duterte) 辩护团队出庭的第一位证人似乎忘记了两件事：他参加了所谓的中国领事馆赞助的 2025 年旅行，以及参议院弹劾法庭可能会以藐视法庭罪指控他。在弹劾审判的第 40 天，达沃市评估员海梅·阿达林 (Jaime Adalin) 对据称于 2025 年 11 月前往中国进行的全费用旅行的看似闪烁其词的回答引起了参议员法官的愤怒。众议院私人检察官杰伊·托洛萨 (Jay Tolosa) 在质疑阿达林早先事件后的可信度时首先提出了这个问题。
content:
副总统萨拉·杜特尔特 (Sara Duterte) 辩护团队出庭的第一位证人似乎忘记了两件事：他参加了所谓的中国领事馆赞助的 2025 年旅行，以及参议院弹劾法庭可能会以藐视法庭罪指控他。在弹劾审判的第 40 天，达沃市评估员杰米·阿达林 (Jaime Adalin) 对据称于 2025 年 11 月前往中国进行的全费用旅行的看似闪烁其词的回答引起了参议员法官的愤怒。众议院自诉检察官杰伊·托洛萨 (Jay Tolosa) 在质疑阿达林先前的闪烁其辞的可信度时首先提出了这个问题。 “你也承认，在2025年11月的某个时候，你是达沃市政府官员之一，在中国领事馆的赞助下前往中国进行全费用旅行？”托洛萨问道。然而，阿达林并没有明确回答，而是笑着驳回了这个问题，说道：“我认为这无关紧要。”这震惊了参议院弹劾法庭，并引起了人群的笑声。 “工程师吉米，你很有趣，”主持人弗朗西斯·“奇兹”·埃斯库德罗告诉阿达林。不过，虽然埃斯库德罗看上去很开心，但其他参议员法官却没那么开心。参议员兼法官维森特·“蒂托”·索托指出，如果阿达林继续声称自己不记得旅行细节，弹劾法庭可以向移民局索取阿达林的旅行记录。
与此同时，参议员法官埃尔文·塔尔福提醒证人，他在宣誓时撒谎或嘲笑诉讼程序可能会被指控藐视法庭。“审判长，证人似乎在愚弄我们。先生，我可以提醒你，你正在宣誓。你现在所做的事情——取笑审判——是被禁止的。我们可以指控你藐视法庭，”塔尔福说。阿达林最终证实，他去年曾以个人名义前往中国。但当被问及 2018 年 11 月是否再次前往该国时，他再次声称自己记不起细节，这引发了参议员兼法官拉菲·塔尔福的再次谴责。 “你想要我给你连你旅行的闭路电视录像吗？2018年11月12日，PR356中国，你在那里呆了两天，”图尔福说。 “你经常出差……我不是批评你，但是你的工资是多少？你怎么总是在国外？”他补充道。参议员兼法官里萨·洪蒂维罗斯也向阿达林询问有关他旅行的详细信息。然而，评估员坚称，他记不起他访问过的地方或哪个机构为这些旅行提供了便利。洪蒂维罗斯说：“先生，我很抱歉，但这可不是闹着玩的。令人难以置信的是，一名工程师、一名城市评估员，自称熟悉辩方和检方提供的地图，却不知道他访问过一个大国的哪些地区。”
阿达林解释说，他并不是特别热衷于旅行，这就是为什么他忘记了旅行的细节。但参议员法官拉菲·图尔福指出了检方质疑的一个更严重的原因：涉嫌从中国汇入汇款。 “你知道，阿达林先生，我们之所以询问你去中国旅行的情况，是因为杜特尔特的丈夫马纳塞斯·卡皮奥律师共同拥有的 Calle88 公司据称从中国和香港向他们汇入了价值 3.19 亿比索的汇款，”图尔福说。他补充说：“听到这个消息并不好……政府官员，特别是那些身居高位的官员，正在接受来自中国的资金，而我们与这个国家有领土争端。”在问题结束时

【原文 English Original】
The first witness presented by the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte appeared to have forgotten two things: his participation in an alleged Chinese consulate-sponsored trip in 2025 and the possibility that the Senate impeachment court could cite him in contempt. On Day 40 of the impeachment trial , Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin drew the ire of senator-judges over his seemingly evasive answers about an alleged all-expenses-paid trip to China in November 2025. House private prosecutor Jay Tolosa first raised the question as he challenged Adalin’s credibility following his earlier evasive answers. “You would also admit that sometime in November 2025, you were one of the LGU officials of Davao who went to China on an all-expenses-paid tour sponsored by the Chinese consulate?” Tolosa asked. However, instead of answering categorically, Adalin laughed and brushed off the question, saying: “I don’t think that’s relevant.” This stunned the Senate impeachment court and drew laughter from the crowd.  “You are funny there, Engineer Jimmy,” presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero told Adalin.  But while Escudero appeared amused, other senator-judges were less entertained. Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto noted that the impeachment court could request Adalin’s travel records from the Bureau of Immigration if he continued to claim he could not remember the details of his trip. Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo , meanwhile, reminded the witness that he could be cited in contempt for lying or making a mockery of the proceedings while under oath. “Presiding Officer, the witness appears to be making a fool of us. Sir, may I remind you that you’re under oath. What you’re doing right now — making fun of the trial — that is prohibited. We can cite you in contempt,” Tulfo said. Adalin eventually confirmed that he had traveled to China on a personal trip last year. But when asked about another trip to the country in November 2018, he again claimed he could no longer remember the details, prompting another rebuke from Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo. “Do you want me to give you even the CCTV footage of your trip? November 12, 2018, PR356 China, you stayed there for two days,” Tulfo said. “You traveled a lot…And I’m not criticizing you, but how much is your salary? How come you are always abroad?” he added. Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros also pressed Adalin for details about his travels. The assessor, however, maintained that he could not recall the places he visited or which agency facilitated the trips. “Sir, I’m sorry but this is no laughing matter. It is unbelievable that an engineer, a city assessor, who claims to be knowledgeable on the maps that the defense and prosecution presented, is unaware of the areas he visited in a large country,” Hontiveros said. Adalin explained that he was not particularly keen on traveling, which was why he had forgotten the details of his trips. But Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo pointed to a more serious reason for the prosecution’s questions: alleged inward remittances from China. “You know, Mr. Adalin, we are asking about your travel to China because Calle88 — a company that Duterte’s husband, Atty. Manases Carpio, co-owns — allegedly sent inward remittances worth P319 million from China and Hong Kong to them,” Tulfo said. “It’s not good to hear that…government officials, especially those in high positions, are receiving money from China, a country that we have a territorial dispute with,” he added. By the end of the questioning, Adalin had managed to recall some details of his trips. Next time, senators are likely to remind him about proper decorum in an impeachment court. – Rappler.com
