title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy
zh_title: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌与中国间谍有染而被国会传唤
summary: 在承认与涉嫌中国间谍的 Megaspeed 高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染后不到 24 小时，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 被要求出席众议院中国问题特别委员会。委员会今天发布了一封信，由众议员布莱恩·J·马斯特 (R-FL)、众议员约翰·莫勒纳尔 (R-MI) 和众议员埃里克·A·克劳福德 (R-AK) 签署。 X 的一篇帖子特别介绍了这封信，指出这封信“表达了对 NVIDIA 针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议的担忧，以及据报道黄先生与新加坡一家与中国情报相关的高管的关系”
content:
在承认与涉嫌中国间谍的 Megaspeed 高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 有染后不到 24 小时，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 被要求出席众议院中国问题特别委员会。委员会今天发布了一封信，由众议员布莱恩·J·马斯特 (R-FL)、众议员约翰·莫勒纳尔 (R-MI) 和众议员埃里克·A·克劳福德 (R-AK) 签署。 X 的一篇帖子特别介绍了这封信，指出这封信“表达了对 NVIDIA 针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议的担忧，以及据报道黄先生与一家新加坡数据中心公司的一名与中国情报相关的高管的关系。” ICYMI：主席@RepMoolenaar、主席@RepBrianMast 和主席@RepRickCrawford 已致函NVIDIA 首席执行官@JensenHuang，要求他本月出席他们的三个委员会的会议。这封信表达了对 NVIDIA 针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议的担忧，以及据报道黄先生与一家新加坡数据中心公司的一名与中国情报相关的高管的关系。 2026 年 11 月 9 日“亲爱的黄先生：我们写信请求您出席我们的委员会，参加一次联合闭门简报会，介绍 NVIDIA 针对外国对手间谍活动的安全协议，以及您与公开报道的中华人民共和国 (PRC) 情报人员：Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 的互动，”信中这样开头。
报告接着说，最近有关该事件的报道“引发了有关中国获取美国敏感技术和信息的重大国家安全担忧。”中国渗透和获取美国尖端技术的问题是本届国会三个委员会调查工作的核心。国会确定美国国家安全面临风险的程度至关重要。”闭门听证会定于 2026 年 11 月 18 日进行；黄是否会出席尚不清楚。这封信还允许黄在第 119 届国会开会期间设定替代日期。周日，黄承认与新加坡 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 有染。据称后者是受中国国家安全部招募来收集信息的并帮助中国获得 Nvidia 的 AI GPU，其中最强大的 GPU 被华盛顿禁止向中国出口。在给 Nvidia 员工的一份声明中，黄仁勋表示，“我欠我的家人和你们所有人一个道歉。我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”正如黄仁勋的声明所指出的，英伟达已对其首席执行官在该报道所暴露的国家安全问题方面的行为展开独立调查。
董事会表示，“虽然董事会没有理由相信国家安全或 NVIDIA 机密遭到泄露，但董事会的调查将检查所有可用信息。”英伟达股价早盘下跌约 5%，但此后已收复部分失地。该公司市值已飙升至超过 4 万亿美元，成为人工智能热潮中的全球硬件领导者。其强大的 GPU 对于人工智能模型的训练和推理都有很高的需求。

【原文 English Original】
Less than 24 hours after he admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese spy , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been asked to appear before the House Select Committee on China. The Committee issued a letter today, signed by Rep. Brian J. Mast (R-FL), Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), and Rep. Eric A. Crawford (R-AK). An X post featuring the letter states that the letter "expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company." ICYMI: Chairman @RepMoolenaar, Chairman @RepBrianMast, and Chairman @RepRickCrawford have sent a letter to NVIDIA CEO @JensenHuang asking him to appear before their three committees this month. The letter expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company. November 9, 2026 "Dear Mr. Huang: We are writing to request that you appear before our committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang," the letter begins. It goes on to say that recent reports surrounding the affair "raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information. "The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk." The closed-door hearing is set for November 18, 2026; whether Huang will attend remains unclear. The letter also allows for Huang to set an alternative date during while the 119th Congress is still in session. On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. It is alleged that the latter was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and help China get its hands on Nvidia's AI GPUs, the most powerful of which are banned from export to the country by Washington. Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion of AI chips into China . In a statement to Nvidia employees, Jensen Huang said, "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." As Huang's statement noted, Nvidia has opened an independent investigation into its CEO's conduct regarding the national security concerns the story has laid bare. The board of directors stated, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." Nvidia shares dropped by around 5% in early trading, but have since recovered some of their losses. The company has rocketed to a market capitalization of over $4 trillion as the global hardware leader of the AI boom. Its powerful GPUs are in high demand for both the training of AI models and inference.

title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
zh_title: 英伟达股价因黄与涉嫌中国间谍的恋情调查而暴跌
summary: 在美国芯片制造商英伟达宣布将对其首席执行官与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情进行独立调查后，该公司的价值已蒸发数千亿美元。在黄仁勋承认婚外情后，该科技公司股价周一收盘下跌约 4%。英伟达发起调查之前有报道称，美国认为中国针对英伟达老板进行了间谍活动。然而，中国否认了这些说法，其外交部表示，有关中国间谍的指控“完全毫无根据”。
content:
在美国芯片制造商英伟达宣布将对其首席执行官与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情进行独立调查后，该公司的价值已蒸发数千亿美元。在黄仁勋承认婚外情后，该科技公司股价周一收盘下跌约 4%。英伟达发起调查之前有报道称，美国认为中国针对英伟达老板进行了间谍活动。然而，中国否认了这些说法，中国外交部表示，有关中国间谍的指控“完全毫无根据，纯属猜测，意在抹黑和诽谤中国”。英伟达表示，没有理由相信该公司的机密或国家安全受到损害，但该公司董事会的一份声明表示，“鉴于最近有报道称创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已成为外国情报工作的目标”，该公司将开始调查。据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报官员认为爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang，又名黄乐）是北京的间谍。报道称，国务卿马可·卢比奥去年春天向华盛顿高级官员发送了一份备忘录，警告英伟达老板与一名中国间谍关系密切。 Alice Huang 是新加坡公司 Megaspeed 的董事总经理，该公司与 Nvidia 有业务往来。黄仁勋承认他对妻子“不忠”，并为伤害她和孩子而道歉。
他补充说，他“致力于保护英伟达并支持美国的国家安全”，并将配合调查。英伟达联合创始人还被要求出席下周几个国会委员会举行的联合闭门简报会。美国众议院外交事务委员会成员上周要求黄仁勋出席闭门简报会，介绍他与爱丽丝·黄的互动以及英伟达围绕间谍活动的安全协议。国会议员布莱恩·马斯特（Brian Mast）、约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar）和里克·克劳福德（Rick Crawford）在一封信中写道：“最近的报告引发了有关中华人民共和国获取美国敏感技术和信息的重大国家安全担忧。” “国会确定美国国家安全面临风险的程度至关重要。”英伟达宣布展开调查后，包括埃隆·马斯克在内的其他大型科技巨头纷纷站出来支持黄仁勋继续领导该公司。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，英伟达的老板是一个“值得尊敬的人”。然而，这一消息引发了英伟达股票的抛售，该公司市值蒸发约 2500 亿美元（1900 亿英镑）。尽管英伟达股价下跌，但美国股市在经历上周的动荡后，本周开盘上涨，英伟达的竞争对手芯片制造商受益。但分析师表示，这种打击将是短暂的。
Crossmark Global Investments 首席市场策略师维多利亚·费尔南德斯 (Victoria Fernandez) 表示，投资者不会放弃英伟达，因为这家芯片制造商对人工智能行业非常重要。“英伟达是人工智能行业的核心，没有他们，所有其他部分都会开始分崩离析，因为融资不存在，”她告诉 BBC。 1993 年，黄仁勋与另外两名工程师共同创立了 Nvidia，该公司在为新兴人工智能技术制造硬件方面发挥着核心作用。该公司的芯片最初是为游戏设计的，但他将重点转向了人工智能开发，将其变成了全球第二大有价值的公司。与其他人不同，黄的地位很脆弱

【原文 English Original】
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia’s probe came after reports that the US believed China had targeted the Nvidia boss in an espionage campaign. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company’s secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm’s board of directors said it would begin an investigation in “light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report . The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia. Jensen Huang admitted he was “unfaithful” to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was “committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security” and would cooperate with the investigation. The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing last week on his interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s security protocols around espionage. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s [China’s] access to sensitive US technology and information,” congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter. “It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk.” After Nvidia announced its investigation, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang continuing to lead the firm. US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an “honourable guy”. However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia’s shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company’s market value. While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened the week on a positive note after last week’s turmoil, with Nvidia’s rival chipmakers benefiting. But analysts suggested the hit would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so important to the AI industry. “Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing’s not there,” she told the BBC. Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia with two other engineers in 1993, and the company is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies. Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but he shifted its focus to AI development, turning it into the world’s second-most valuable company. Huang’s position vulnerable unlike other tech bosses A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Jensen Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was “no natural successor” to the chief executive. Unlike other tech founders, Jensen Huang is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia’s board of directors to oust him. He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single-class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision. By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies. Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Jensen Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, “but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future.” The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched. Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold. Washington previously restricted the H200, Nvidia’s second most advanced semiconductor, over concerns that it would give China’s technology industry an edge over the US. But Jensen Huang has opposed restrictions on selling Nvidia’s chips to China, arguing that the global rollout of AI would be better powered by US technology. In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.

title: Hong Kong must reform ticketing and venue rules to attract touring mega-acts, think tank says
zh_title: 智囊团表示，香港必须改革票务和场地规则以吸引大型巡演
summary: 一家智库发现，近年来大多数西方艺术家的巡演都跳过了香港，香港必须加强票务系统，确保主办方能够找到吸引巡演艺术家的场地。 2024 年 12 月 1 日，Clockenflap 的观众。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港未来经济研究所周一发布的一份报告分析了2023年至2026年间95位西方艺术家的巡回演唱会，其中只有21.1%包括香港。几乎一半的旅行团包括新加坡，占 49.5%，而东京则占近四分之三的旅行团，占 7%
content:
一家智库发现，近年来大多数西方艺术家的巡演都跳过了香港，香港必须加强票务系统，确保主办方能够找到吸引巡演艺术家的场地。 2024 年 12 月 1 日，Clockenflap 的观众。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港未来经济研究所周一发布的一份报告分析了2023年至2026年间95位西方艺术家的巡回演唱会，其中只有21.1%包括香港。几乎一半的旅行团包括新加坡，占 49.5%，而东京则占近四分之三的旅行团，占 74.7%。 “艾德·希兰 (Ed Sheeran) 在一次巡演中演奏了 16 个亚洲城市，但没有在香港演出；杜阿·利帕 (Dua Lipa) 演奏了 8 个城市。总共 95 场西方巡演中，有 75 场不包括香港，”它说。报告还指出，自启德体育场启用以来，“数据显示香港的地位没有明显改善”，并指出截至 2026 年 9 月，酷玩乐队是唯一一家在该场地演出的西方乐队。照片：塞巴斯蒂安·纳吉。报道撰写时，加拿大歌手 The Weeknd 尚未在体育场演出。上个月，他在该场地继续进行了四场演出，场场门票全部售空，其中他的新歌《香港》（采样了粤语流行偶像王菲 1993 年的歌曲）登上了当地排行榜的榜首。
报告称，不断增加的票务欺诈和较短的场地预订窗口是导致香港落后于区域竞争对手的“弱点”。报告称，“香港拥有活动之都的资产：强有力的政策支持、国际连通性和主要的新场馆。然而，这些优势尚未转化为国际西方旅游的可比份额。” “观众需要能够放心地购买门票，主办方需要在协调跨城市的日期的同时确保合适的场地。我们的审查发现了这两方面的弱点。”另请参阅：文化负责人表示，在新加坡将主办 Lady Gaga 的消息传出后，香港正努力引进大型国际活动 该报告指出，2024 年至 2025 年间，演唱会门票欺诈案件增加了 62%，而消费者委员会有关公开演出的投诉激增了 202%，同期从 626 起增加到 1,889 起。报告称，机器人购买和倒卖行为，以及对这些行为的控制和执行薄弱，也可能破坏了“粉丝和组织者所需的可靠性和透明度”。该协会还表示，红磡香港体育馆等政府运营场地的预订规则“不太适合”国际巡演，因为音乐会的预订期限为 12 个月，而且缺乏临时举行制度。香港启德体育公园。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
该研究所建议政府通过提高倒票罚款、公布门票分配数据和升级平台基础设施来实现票务和消费者保护安排的现代化。它还敦促引入两年预订窗口，为国际申请提供明确的评估标准，并提供免费的临时保留，并呼吁公布批准时间表和预订结果。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong must step up its ticketing systems and ensure promoters can secure venues to attract touring artists, a think tank has said, after finding that most Western artists’ tours skipped the city in recent years. Audience members at Clockenflap, on December 1, 2024. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Out of 95 Western artists’ concert tours between 2023 and 2026 analysed in a report published on Monday by the Hong Kong Future Economy Institute, just 21.1 per cent included Hong Kong. Almost half of the tours included Singapore, at 49.5 per cent, while Tokyo was on almost three-quarters of the tours, at 74.7 per cent. “Ed Sheeran played sixteen Asian cities on one tour without a Hong Kong date; Dua Lipa played eight. In total, 75 of the 95 Western tours did not include Hong Kong,” it said. ‘Weaknesses on both fronts’ The report also stated that “the data shows no clear improvement in Hong Kong’s position” since the opening of Kai Tak Stadium, noting that Coldplay was the sole Western act to have played the venue as of September 2026. The Weeknd in Hong Kong. Photo: Sebastian Nagy. Canadian singer The Weeknd had not yet performed at the stadium when the report was compiled. He went on to play four sold-out shows at the venue last month, with his new track “Hong Kong” — which samples a 1993 song by Cantopop icon Faye Wong — topping local charts. Rising ticketing fraud and short venue booking windows are “weaknesses” that have contributed to the lag behind the city’s regional rivals, the report said. “Hong Kong has the assets of an events capital: strong policy backing, international connectivity and major new venues. Yet these strengths have not translated into a comparable share of international Western tours,” it said. “Audiences need to be able to buy tickets with confidence, and promoters need to secure suitable venues while coordinating dates across cities. Our review identifies weaknesses on both fronts.” See also: Hong Kong striving to bring in large-scale int’l events, says culture chief amid word that Singapore to host Lady Gaga The report cited a 62 per cent rise in concert ticket fraud cases between 2024 and 2025, alongside a 202 per cent surge in Consumer Council complaints regarding public performances, rising from 626 to 1,889 over the same period. Bot purchases and scalping — as well as weak controls and enforcement against those practices — may also have undermined “the reliability and transparency that fans and organisers need,” the report said. The institute also said that booking rules at government-run venues such as the Hong Kong Coliseum in Hung Hom were “poorly suited” for international tours, pointing to the 12-month window for booking concerts and the lack of a provisional holding system. Hong Kong’s Kai Tak Sports Park. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The institute recommended that the government modernise ticketing and consumer protection arrangements by raising scalping fines, publishing ticket allocation data, and upgrading platform infrastructure. It also urged the introduction of a two-year booking window with clear evaluation criteria for international applications, alongside cost-free provisional holds, and called for the publication of approval timelines and booking outcomes.

title: The Jensen Huang spy scandal is becoming a White House problem
zh_title: 黄仁勋间谍丑闻正在成为白宫问题
summary: 困扰英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻不再仅仅是硅谷最有权势的人之一是否与涉嫌中国间谍有染的问题。这也是一个关于白宫知道什么以及它可能选择忽视什么的问题。在《纽约时报》的爆炸性报道之后，黄仁勋和英伟达于周日证实了这一关系。爆料的核心女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司是 Nvidia 芯片的主要客户。据报道，美国情报监视显示，她一直在向我输送信息。
content:
困扰英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻不再仅仅是硅谷最有权势的人之一是否与涉嫌中国间谍有染的问题。这也是一个关于白宫知道什么以及它可能选择忽视什么的问题。在《纽约时报》的爆炸性报道之后，黄仁勋和英伟达于周日证实了这一关系。爆料的核心女性爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司是 Nvidia 芯片的主要客户。据报道，美国情报监视显示，她一直在直接向中国政府提供信息。目前尚不清楚的是，有多少敏感信息可能被泄露，黄对他所见的那个女人了解多少，以及为什么美国情报官员显然没有警告他她涉嫌与北京的关系。这些答案可能会对黄和白宫造成严重损害。乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心研究员萨姆·布雷斯尼克表示：“很多人都清楚他将成为中国情报收集的目标。”鉴于黄与特朗普关系密切，而且他领导的公司是“中美人工智能竞争的核心”。英伟达不断变化的故事 承认这件事也与英伟达和黄本人之前描述他与爱丽丝黄的关系的方式相矛盾。
就在 10 月 29 日，公司发言人约翰·里佐 (John Rizzo) 将他们的互动描述为例行业务往来，而黄坚称这些互动“完全正常，并不罕见”。黄现在面临英伟达董事会的调查，尽管董事们在周日的声明中表示，他们“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密受到损害”，并表示“对詹森及其领导团队充满信心”。董事会的调查可能是黄仁勋最不担心的事情。这位有权势的首席执行官面临着国会两党审查的前景，同时人们对他在华盛顿的影响力以及他在英伟达的未来也提出了越来越多的质疑。国会想要回答的问题 国会已经开始提出问题。上周晚些时候，三名众议院议员——共和党人布莱恩·马斯特(Brian Mast)、约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)和埃里克·克劳福德(Eric Crawford)——给黄致了一封信，要求他出席在华盛顿就此事举行的闭门听证会。周一，当被《Fast Company》问及黄仁勋是否打算参加时，英伟达拒绝公开回应。明年，民主党控制的新国会可能会传唤包括黄仁勋在内的一些科技领袖就他们与特朗普的往来作证。周一，特拉华州参议员克里斯·库恩斯 (Chris Coons) 呼吁对黄仁勋和英伟达进行调查，以确定国家安全是否受到损害。 “我们需要关于人工智能亿万富翁和特朗普政府之间关系的答案，”他在 X 上写道。
当民主党一月份控制国会时，库恩斯将担任参议院外交关系委员会主席，这赋予他相当大的权力来寻求这些答案。当然还有很多事情需要调查。我们还有很多不知道的事情，而出现的情况可能会对黄和白宫造成严重损害。其一，我们不知道 Alice Huang 是否从黄仁勋那里获取了敏感信息并将其传输给中国政府。布雷斯尼克说，黄和他的设备可能拥有多种有价值的信息。这可能包括贸易

【原文 English Original】
The scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is no longer simply a question of whether one of Silicon Valley’s most powerful men had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. It’s also a question of what the White House knew—and what it might have chosen to overlook. Huang and Nvidia confirmed the relationship Sunday, following a bombshell New York Times report . Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the revelations, is an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, a major customer of Nvidia chips. U.S. intelligence surveillance reportedly showed that she had been funneling information directly to the Chinese government. What remains unclear is how much sensitive information may have been compromised, what Huang knew about the woman he was seeing, and why U.S. intelligence officials apparently failed to warn him about her suspected ties to Beijing. The answers could prove deeply damaging to both Huang and the White House. “It was pretty clear to a lot of people that he would be a target of Chinese intelligence collection,” says Sam Bresnick, a research fellow at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, given Huang’s proximity to Trump and his leadership of a company that is “central to the U.S.-China AI competition.” Nvidia’s changing story The admission of the affair also contradicts how Nvidia and Huang himself had previously characterized his ties to Alice Huang. As recently as October 29, company spokesperson John Rizzo described their interactions as routine business dealings, while Huang insisted they were “completely normal and not unusual.” Huang now faces an investigation by Nvidia’s board, although directors said in a Sunday statement that they had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised” and expressed “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The board’s investigation may be the least of Huang’s worries. The powerful CEO faces the prospect of bipartisan congressional scrutiny, along with mounting questions about his influence in Washington and his future at Nvidia. The questions Congress wants answered Already, Congress has begun asking questions. Late last week, three House members—Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Eric Crawford—sent Huang a letter requesting that he attend a closed-door hearing on the matter in Washington. Asked by Fast Company on Monday whether Huang intends to attend, Nvidia declined to answer on the record. Next year, the new Democrat-controlled Congress will likely call a number of tech leaders, including Huang, to testify about their dealings with Trump. On Monday, Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware called for an investigation into Huang and Nvidia to determine whether national security had been compromised. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration,” he wrote on X. Coons is poised to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January, giving him considerable power to pursue those answers. There is certainly plenty to investigate. There is still much we don’t know, and what emerges could prove deeply damaging to both Huang and the White House. For one, we don’t know whether Alice Huang obtained sensitive information from Jensen Huang and transmitted it to the Chinese government. Huang and his devices may have been in possession of several types of valuable information, says Bresnick. That could include trade secrets about upcoming Nvidia chips, the company’s research strategies, or U.S. government plans to restrict China’s access to advanced AI technology. “Did he provide information to her about the Trump administration’s thinking on AI—U.S.-China competition, export controls, and trade policy more broadly?” Bresnick asks. “Because if they have greater texture on what the administration’s thinking, it’s easier for them to position themselves.” (The White House did not respond to Fast Company ‘s request for comment.) It’s also unclear what Huang knew about Alice Huang, and when. He certainly knew he was having an affair with an executive at a customer company, in violation of Nvidia’s code of conduct. But we don’t know when he learned that she was a suspected spy. Why didn’t Huang run a background check on her, Bresnick asks, or consult U.S. intelligence agencies? What did the White House know? Then there’s the question of when U.S. intelligence learned about Alice Huang’s activities. According to the reporting, the U.S. government had known about Alice Huang’s ties to Beijing for months. Bresnick finds it strange that intelligence officials apparently failed to warn Jensen Huang, given his close relationship with the president and his position atop a company developing some of the world’s most advanced AI technology. “The fact that this potentially could have been at risk” makes the apparent lack of intervention all the more puzzling, he says. One possibility is that the White House prevented intelligence agencies from warning Huang about the suspected spy. The Trump administration, after all, has compelling reasons to keep Huang and Nvidia out of the headlines. The stock market’s strong performance has been a central selling point for the administration, and Nvidia is the crown jewel of the AI-related stocks that have driven much of its growth. AI and AI-related companies accounted for as much as half of the market’s gains this year, according to a new J.P. Morgan report . The White House may have had an even more direct financial incentive. The federal government stands to collect revenue from Nvidia’s AI chip sales to China. Last year, Huang persuaded Trump to allow Nvidia to sell its H200 chips in China, provided the U.S. government received a 25% cut of the sales. Huang also reportedly discussed selling Nvidia’s top-of-the-line Blackwell GPUs in China, but that proposal was ultimately shut down over national-security concerns. In August 2025, Huang agreed to give the U.S. government a 15% cut in exchange for permission to sell the lower-performing H20 chip to China. “Was the government hoping to get a bunch of money from these deals, from Chinese buyers getting access to these things?” Bresnick asks. Why Huang may stick around at Nvidia These questions raise the possibility of a cover-up motivated by financial or political considerations, though there is no evidence yet that the administration deliberately withheld information from Huang. Still, corruption was a major factor in voters’ decisions in the midterms, and Nvidia now risks becoming entangled in a controversy that could damage its standing in Washington. But Creative Strategies chairman and longtime analyst Tim Bajarin suggests those calling for Huang’s ouster could meet serious opposition. “Removal of Jensen would be a very difficult decision because he is the heart and soul of Nvidia,” Bajarin says. “I have met with Jensen many times over the years, and he was always the smartest guy in the room. More importantly, he has the global vision for Nvidia’s future and needs to be the one driving their future.”

David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.

台湾10月出口创高位 人工智能需求猛增近60%
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
台湾财政部。 CNA档案照片
中新社台北11月9日电 台湾财政部周一表示，由于全球对人工智能(AI)应用的强劲需求持续推动科技产品出货量，台湾10月份出口创历史新高，同比增长近60%。
财政部数据显示，9月份出口同比增长58.9%至967.6亿美元，打破了9月872.2亿美元的历史纪录，进口增长75.1%至688.9亿美元。
台湾地区贸易顺差278.8亿美元，同比增长29.4%。
财政部表示，10月份出口连续第36个月同比增长。
2026年前10个月，台湾出口额同比增长47.7%至7582.9亿美元，进口额增长44.6%至5697.6亿美元。
前10个月贸易顺差1885.4亿美元，同比增长57.7%。
财政部将强劲的出口表现主要归因于对人工智能基础设施的大量投资，这推动了对人工智能相关产品的需求。
商务部表示，10月份，信息、通信和音像制品出口同比增长72.9%，达到创纪录的476亿美元。
电子元件出口额也创历史新高，达到326.8亿美元，同比增长61.4%，其中集成电路出口额增长63.0%，达到311.7亿美元。
根据财政部的数据，这两个行业合计占台湾 10 月份出口总额的 83%。
财政部称，大多数传统行业的出口也较上年大幅增长。
由于芯片制造商扩大产能，半导体生产设备出货量增加，10月份机械出口同比增长35.5%，达到28.8亿美元。
财政部表示，基本金属出口也同比增长35.7%，达到28.8亿美元。
从目的地来看，美国10月份仍是台湾最大的出口市场，由于科技产品的需求不断增长，出货量同比增长55.9%，达到创纪录的329.3亿美元。
当月台湾出口总额中，美国占34%。
中国和香港位列第二，采购台湾商品204.4亿美元，同比增长42.9%；其次是东南亚国家联盟（ASEAN），出口总额184.6亿美元，增长83.8%。
财政部统计司司长蔡美娜告诉记者，2026年前10个月，美国对台湾出口占比达31.7%，为36年来最高。
与此同时，对中国大陆和香港的出口合计份额下降至 23.8%，为 27 年来的最低水平，她说。
蔡崇信将这些变化主要归因于中美贸易紧张局势以及对人工智能等技术的需求不断增长导致的全球供应链的变化。
随着人工智能需求持续推动出货量，财政部预测11月台湾出口额将达到942亿美元至967亿美元，同比增长47%至51%。

【原文 English Original】
Taiwan's October exports hit high, jump nearly 60% on AI demand - Focus Taiwan
Taiwan's October exports hit high, jump nearly 60% on AI demand
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taiwan's Ministry of Finance. CNA file photo
Taipei, Nov. 9 (CNA) Taiwan's exports hit a record high in October, surging nearly 60 percent from a year earlier as strong global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications continued to boost shipments of technology products, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said Monday.
MOF data showed that exports rose 58.9 percent year-on-year to US$96.76 billion, smashing the previous record of US$87.22 billion in September, while imports increased 75.1 percent to US$68.89 billion.
Taiwan recorded a trade surplus of US$27.88 billion, up 29.4 percent from a year earlier.
October marked the 36th consecutive month of year-on-year export growth, the MOF said.
In the first 10 months of 2026, Taiwan's exports rose 47.7 percent from a year earlier to US$758.29 billion, while imports increased 44.6 percent to US$569.76 billion.
The trade surplus for the 10-month period reached US$188.54 billion, up 57.7 percent year-on-year.
The MOF attributed the strong export performance largely to massive investment in AI infrastructure, which drove demand for AI-related products.
In October, exports of information, communications, and audiovisual products surged 72.9 percent from a year earlier to a record US$47.60 billion, the ministry said.
Exports of electronic components also hit a record US$32.68 billion, up 61.4 percent year-on-year, with integrated circuit exports rising 63.0 percent to US$31.17 billion.
Together, the two sectors accounted for 83 percent of Taiwan's total exports in October, according to the MOF.
Exports from most traditional industries also largely increased from a year earlier, according to the MOF.
Machinery exports rose 35.5 percent from a year earlier to US$2.88 billion in October, driven by increased shipments of semiconductor production equipment as chipmakers expanded capacity.
Exports of base metals also increased 35.7 percent year-on-year to US$2.88 billion, the MOF said.
By destination, the United States remained Taiwan's largest export market in October, with shipments rising 55.9 percent from a year earlier to a record US$32.93 billion amid growing demand for technology products.
The U.S. accounted for 34 percent of Taiwan's total exports during the month.
China and Hong Kong ranked second, purchasing US$20.44 billion worth of Taiwanese goods, up 42.9 percent year-on-year, followed by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), with exports totaling US$18.46 billion, an increase of 83.8 percent.
MOF Department of Statistics Director-General Beatrice Tsai (蔡美娜) told reporters that the U.S. accounted for 31.7 percent of Taiwan's exports in the first 10 months of 2026, its highest share in 36 years.
Meanwhile, the combined share of exports going to China and Hong Kong fell to 23.8 percent, its lowest level in 27 years, she said.
Tsai attributed the changes largely to shifts in global supply chains amid U.S.-China trade tensions and the growing demand for technologies such as AI.
With AI demand continuing to drive shipments, the MOF forecast Taiwan's exports would reach between US$94.2 billion and US$96.7 billion in November, representing year-on-year growth of 47 percent to 51 percent.
For 2026 as a whole, Tsai said Taiwan's exports were expected to exceed US$900 billion, surpassing previous records.

content:
周一，在安塔利亚召开的第 31 届联合国气候变化框架公约缔约方会议 (COP31) 上，非洲谈判小组 (AGN) 敦促世界领导人发出果断呼吁，COP31 必须标志着从谈判承诺到切实财政交付的最终过渡。 AGN 主席 Nana Antwi-Boasiako Amoah 博士在安塔利亚开幕全体会议上代表非洲大陆发言，强调非洲履行其气候承诺的能力完全取决于立即动员更多、可预测的气候融资。阿莫阿博士将非洲集团与 77 国集团和中国保持一致，宣布以实施为重点的峰会必须是在金融方面取得成果的峰会，为土耳其主办、澳大利亚主持谈判的为期两周的谈判定下了坚定的基调。 AGN 主席在发言中首先祝贺即将上任的土耳其主席国，并对澳大利亚和贝伦即将卸任的巴西主席国表示感谢，并阐明了非洲大陆面临的严峻悖论。非洲对全球温室气体排放的贡献最小，但受到气候引起的破坏的影响却尤为严重。尽管非洲国家已经提交了雄心勃勃的国家自主贡献（NDC）和国家适应计划（NAP），但阿莫阿博士强调，这一雄心壮志的绝大多数仍然被未兑现的财务承诺所束缚。
他强调，如果没有承诺的实施手段，非洲国家就无法实施气候减缓和适应战略，从而将气候融资从次要讨论项目转变为安塔利亚所有全球进展的必要先决条件。“非洲来到安塔利亚传达了一个明确的信息：实施取决于实施手段。我们的大陆对这场危机的贡献最小，也是受其影响最大的大陆之一。非洲国家提出了雄心勃勃的国家自主贡献和适应计划，但大部分雄心取决于尚未到位的资金，”纳纳说阿莫阿。将非洲优先事项纳入官方议程 为了确保核心财务和结构优先事项正式纳入 COP31 议程，非洲集团推动纳入三个关键补充议程项目。在开幕式凌晨结束的激烈的代表团团长谈判之后，阿莫阿博士宣布，已就将这些优先事项纳入正式议程达成共识。
这些目标是： 实施并跟踪适应资金流量增加两倍的进展情况，以解决发展中国家日益严重的脆弱性问题；评估单边贸易相关气候措施对发展中经济体的影响，根据《公约》第 3.5 条保护非洲工业化；在即将进行的第三次增资之前，对绿色气候基金所需和可用的资金进行正式评估。就贸易和气候变化进行专门对话的需求是非洲经济体的一个关键问题。随着单边贸易法规和碳边界调整在全球范围内激增，阿莫阿博士警告说，此类措施有可能将绿色转型的财政负担转移给发展中国家，从而损害当地工业发展，这与《联合国气候变化框架公约》第3.5条直接矛盾。此外，AGN 主席强调有必要评估 f

【原文 English Original】
COP31 must mark the definitive transition from negotiated promises to tangible financial delivery, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) has urged world leaders in a decisive call as the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) opened in Antalya on Monday. Speaking on behalf of the continent at the opening plenary in Antalya, AGN Chair, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, emphasised that Africa’s ability to fulfil its climate commitments rests entirely on the immediate mobilisation of scaled-up, predictable climate finance. Aligning the African bloc with the Group of 77 and China, Dr Amoah declared that an implementation-focused summit must be a summit that delivers on finance, setting a firm tone for the two-week negotiations hosted by Türkiye, with Australia presiding over negotiations. Opening the intervention with congratulations to the incoming Turkish Presidency and gratitude to Australia and the outgoing Brazilian Presidency from Belém, the AGN Chair articulated the stark paradox facing the African continent. Africa contributes the least to global greenhouse gas emissions yet suffers disproportionately from climate-induced disruptions. While African nations have submitted highly ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), Dr. Amoah highlighted that the vast majority of this ambition remains locked behind unfulfilled financial pledges. He stressed that African countries cannot carry out climate mitigation and adaptation strategies without the promised means of implementation, transforming climate finance from a secondary discussion item into the essential prerequisite for all global progress in Antalya. “Africa comes to Antalya with one clear message: implementation depends on means of implementation. Our continent contributes the least to this crisis and is among the most exposed to its impacts. African countries have put forward ambitious NDCs and adaptation plans, but most of that ambition depends on finance that has not yet arrived,” said Nana Amoah. Adoption of Africa’s priorities in official agenda To ensure that core financial and structural priorities were formally integrated into the COP31 proceedings, the African Group pushed for the inclusion of three key supplementary agenda items. Following intense Head of Delegation negotiations that concluded in the early hours of the opening morning, Dr Amoah announced that consensus had been reached to adopt these priorities into the official agenda. These are to: operationalise and track progress toward tripling adaptation finance flows to address growing vulnerability across developing states; evaluate the impact of unilateral trade-related climate measures on developing economies, protecting African industrialisation under Article 3.5 of the Convention; and conduct a formal assessment of funding necessary and available for the Green Climate Fund ahead of its upcoming third replenishment. The demand for a dedicated dialogue on trade and climate change represents a pivotal issue for African economies. As unilateral trade regulations and carbon border adjustments proliferate globally, Dr Amoah warned that such measures threaten to shift the financial burden of the green transition onto developing nations, undermining local industrial development in direct contradiction to Article 3.5 of the UNFCCC Convention. Additionally, the AGN Chair underscored the necessity of evaluating the financial requirements of the Green Climate Fund (GCF). As the GCF prepares for its third replenishment cycle, the African Group called on the COP to fulfil existing commitments by assessing the exact scale of resources needed to meet developing countries’ actual climate requirements. The position outlined by the AGN Chair reflects a unified stance across the Global South, backed by key negotiating coalitions including the Arab Group, the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), the Independent Association of Latin America and the Caribbean (AILAC), and the broader G77 and China alliance chaired by Uruguay. This collective push comes against the backdrop of alarming contractions in global climate finance. Contextual statements delivered on behalf of the G77 and China highlighted that the Global Environment Facility’s ninth replenishment (GEF-9) suffered a 27 percent decline compared to GEF-8, marking its lowest funding level in 16 years. Concurrently, major developed nations have announced reductions that cut their signed GCF contributions for 2024–2027 by half. These declines coincide with massive shortfalls in loss and damage funding, where funding requests exceed available resources by over eightfold. Operationalising equity and industrial growth For the African Group, the ultimate measure of success at COP31 will be an outcome that balances mitigation ambition with robust financial delivery, equity, and common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC). Dr Amoah reiterated that low-carbon and climate-resilient transitions must foster equitable, shared prosperity, providing African nations with the necessary policy space to industrialise, expand energy access, and eradicate poverty. By securing adoption of its agenda items through collaborative Head of Delegation negotiations, the African Group has positioned financial accountability and trade equity at the core of the Antalya summit. As committee sessions and ministerial roundtables begin across the Antalya Expo Centre, the AGN Chair’s call serves as a focal point for developing nations demanding that international climate governance shift permanently from pledge-making to guaranteed delivery.

content:
MAGGIE HABERMAN, JONATHAN SWAN, JULIAN E. BARNES, TRIPP MICKLE2026年11月9日
今年春天，一份备忘录在特朗普政府高层官员中传阅，警告称英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名中国间谍关系密切。 Lisi Niesner/Reuters
多位听取了相关简报的人士表示，今年春天，国务卿马尔科·鲁比奥监督起草了一份高度机密的备忘录，向特朗普政府高层发出警告，指出英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名中国间谍关系密切。
该文件基于对中国公民黄乐（音，英文名Alice Huang)进行电子监控所获取的机密情报。她是一家新加坡公司高管，该公司当时正采购英伟达的先进人工智能芯片，并因涉嫌将这些芯片非法走私至中国而接受调查。美国官员已得出结论，黄女士与这位英伟达掌门人（两人无亲属关系）关系密切，且她已被中国最高情报机构国家安全部招募为间谍。
鲁比奥参与向政府官员通报情况一事此前未被报道。这凸显出高级官员已经知晓这段关系及对间谍活动的担忧，尽管黄仁勋作为AI爆炸性增长的一个关键人物，在相关政策上至今仍能对特朗普施加重要影响力。
黄仁勋一直反对对最先进人工智能芯片出口实施更严格监管，并积极推动将除最新研发技术以外的所有技术出售给中国。在全球争夺人工智能主导权的角逐中，中国是美国的主要竞争对手。
周日，英伟达表示，在黄仁勋承认曾与黄女士有亲密关系后，公司正对他展开调查，不过该公司也表示“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密遭到了泄露”。
“我对妻子不忠，”他说，“我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深表歉意。”
听取了简报的人士称，在特朗普5月访华前，鲁比奥的备忘录被分发给了拥有高级别安全权限的政府官员。因讨论敏感材料，这些人士要求匿名。
尽管是人工智能领域的先驱，也是全球最具价值公司之一的掌门人，但黄仁勋最初并未被列入受邀陪同特朗普访华的主要商业和科技高管名单中。目前尚不清楚这一决定是否与该备忘录有关。听取了简报的人士表示，那时政府内部已有一些人对黄仁勋影响政策的能力感到担忧——总统对人工智能仅实施了轻度的监管。
看到媒体关于黄仁勋缺席代表团的报道后，特朗普总统要求他在阿拉斯加中转期间与“空军一号”会合，以此加入此次行程。总统起草了一篇社交媒体帖子，称很荣幸能有“伟大的黄仁勋”和其他商业领袖“前往伟大的中国，在那里我将请求杰出非凡的领导人习近平主席‘开放’中国，以便这些才华横溢的人能够施展他们的魔力。”
《纽约时报》上个月报道称，特朗普在大约一年前曾听取简报，得知美国情报界对黄女士进行了电子监控，并认为她是效力于中国情报机构的特工。监控显示黄女士与一名美国公民关系密切。当官员们要求“揭示”该美国公民的姓名时（美国人的身份通常受到保护以免受涉外情报监控），结果显示此人正是英伟达首席执行官。
总统当时选择不采取任何行动。他一直将英伟达的芯片视为美国在人工智能领域对华竞争中不可或缺的一部分，并认为英伟达的成功是维持股市强劲势头的关键。
曾与黄乐会面的人士透露，她英语流利，并与人工智能芯片行业的最高层高管保持着关系，其中包括黄仁勋以及英伟达超级计算机顶级组装商之一技嘉的领导人。
目前尚不清楚黄乐是何时结识这位英伟达领导人的。2024年，大约在他们两人与其他行业高管在台北一家酒吧被拍到合影的同时，她的公司Megaspeed开始了价值数十亿美元的先进人工智能微芯片采购计划。
英伟达高管表示，黄仁勋与黄女士的互动“并不反常或出人意料”，且与他同英伟达众多客户中任何一位会面的情况一致。该公司还表示，像Megaspeed这样的客户不会接触到机密商业信息。
近年来，Megaspeed尽管实质上只有一个门面办公室，在当地几乎没有业务足迹，却采购了价值20亿美元的英伟达产品。Megaspeed在东南亚建设数据中心，将其算力出租给中国互联网巨头阿里巴巴。美国官员怀疑，Megaspeed一直在协助将受限的先进英伟达芯片走私至中国。

title: China builds massive 800-megawatt AI data center campus to rival US Stargate project
zh_title: 中国建设大型800兆瓦人工智能数据中心园区，与美国星际之门项目相媲美
summary: 根据 SemiAnalysis 的一份新报告，中国正在内蒙古建设一个 800MW 的人工智能数据中心园区，这可能会挑战美国 Stargate 项目的经济性。 Envision 在不到一年的时间里建成了第一个 120 MW 的 Galaxy AI 数据中心园区，研究人员在 9 月份访问该地点后，其成本仅为美国同类项目的五分之一。但建造建筑物只是成功的一半。人工智能数据中心需要大量的电力，而远景能源正在采取一种不同寻常的方式来保护它——建造自己的风电场和电池存储。
content:
根据 SemiAnalysis 的一份新报告，中国正在内蒙古建设一个 800MW 的人工智能数据中心园区，这可能会挑战美国 Stargate 项目的经济性。 Envision 在不到一年的时间里建成了第一个 120 MW 的 Galaxy AI 数据中心园区，研究人员在 9 月份访问该地点后，其成本仅为美国同类项目的五分之一。但建造建筑物只是成功的一半。人工智能数据中心需要大量电力，而远景能源正在采取一种不同寻常的方式来确保其安全——在计算设施旁边建造自己的风电场和电池存储。当美国开发商转向现场燃气轮机来解决电网限制时，远景能源正在与风电场、电池存储和专用电力基础设施一起建设数据中心。银河位于内蒙古乌兰察布市，正在为两家未具名的互联网公司分四个阶段进行开发。竣工园区计划到 2027 年底提供高达 800MW 的 IT 容量，接近德克萨斯州阿比林 Stargate 园区约 820MW 的关键 IT 容量。远景能源正在为 Galaxy 建设自己的电源，而不是把一切都交给当地电网。到目前为止，该公司已安装了超过100GW的风力涡轮机，并希望其风电场能够提供园区前两期所需电力的60%以上。
这些发电场相距约 80 公里，总装机容量为 420 兆瓦。这远远高于前两期预计的 240 兆瓦负载，尽管风力涡轮机很少能全速运行。乌兰察布的风能系数在 355% 到 40% 之间，因此远景集团增加了四个小时的电池存储，以便在风停时保持电力供应。 （图片来源：SemiAnalysis）事实证明，对于一些美国数据中心建设者来说，获得电力设备相当困难。我们之前曾报道过涡轮机短缺，导致交付预计推迟到 2030 年，而 SpaceX 正在寻求为其燃气动力人工智能设施制造自己的涡轮叶片。与此同时，远景能源正在将风力发电和电池存储与服务器放在一起。 Galaxy 内部的电源硬件也值得一看。 Semianalyss 参观了一个 5MW 大厅，其中固态变压器将 10kV 交流电直接转换为 800V 直流电，供服务器机架使用。这与传统的数据中心配电有很大不同，传统的数据中心配电通常涉及多个中间转换阶段。研究人员写道：“在一个 5MW 大厅中，我们看到 800V 系统正在工作。”
他们解释说，“固态变压器 (SST) 从电网获取 10kV 交流电，并将其直接转换为机架的 800V 直流电。”该设计消除了传统数据中心电源系统中的几个中间组件，包括低压变压器、不间断电源和整流器。尽管 SemiAnalysis 没有为 Galaxy 试点提供可测量的效率改进，但较少的转换级可以降低设备要求和能源损失。 5MW 装置仅占园区的一小部分，但它使该技术在实际设施中投入运行。然而，Envision 计划在下一个建设阶段进行更大规模的部署，此举与 Nvidia 在未来高密度 AI 系统中推动 800V 直流配电的举措相一致。 Galaxy 园区采用液冷和风冷服务器共享的冷却布置

【原文 English Original】
China is building an 800MW AI data center campus in Inner Mongolia that could challenge the economics of America's Stargate project, according to a new report from SemiAnalysis . Envision has built the first 120 MW of Galaxy AI data center campus in less than a year, a cost the researchers put at just one-fifth of comparable US projects, after visiting the site in September. But getting the buildings up is only half of the battle. AI data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, and Envision is taking an unusual route to secure it— building its own wind farms and battery storage alongside the computing facility. While US developers are turning to on-site gas turbines to work around grid constraints, Envision is building its data center alongside wind farms, battery storage, and dedicated power infrastructure. Galaxy is located in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, and is being developed across four phases for two unnamed internet companies. The completed campus is planned to provide up to 800MW of IT capacity by the end of 2027, putting it closer to the approximately 820MW of critical IT capacity at the Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas. Envision is building its own power supply for Galaxy rather than leaving everything to the local grid. So far, the company has installed more than 100GW of wind turbines and wants its wind farms to provide over 60% of the electricity needed by the campus’s first two phases. Those farms, located about 80 kilometers apart, have a combined capacity of 420MW. That's well above the 240MW load expected from the first two phases, although wind turbines rarely get to run flat out. Ulanqab’s wind capacity factor is between 355 and 40%, so Envision is adding four-hour battery storage to keep the electricity coming when the wind dies down. (Image credit: SemiAnalysis) Power equipment is proving rather hard to come by for some US data center builders. We have previously reported on turbine shortages that have pushed delivery estimates to 2030, while SpaceX is looking to manufacture its own turbine blades for its gas-powered AI facilities. Envision, meanwhile, is putting wind generation and battery storage right alongside its servers. The power hardware inside the Galaxy is worth a look, too. Semianalyss visited a 5MW hall where solid-state transformers take 10kV AC electricity and convert it directly into 800V DC for the server racks. That's a fairly substantial departure from conventional data-center power distribution, which typically involves several intermediate conversion stages. “In one 5MW hall, we saw the 800V system at work,” the researchers wrote. They explained that “Solid-state transformers (SSTs) take 10kV AC from the grid and convert it straight to 800V DC for the racks.” The design removes several intermediate components found in conventional data center power systems, including low voltage transformers, uninterruptible power supplies and rectifiers. Fewer conversion stages can reduce equipment requirements and energy losses, although SemiAnalysis did not provide a measured efficiency improvement for Galaxy’s pilot. The 5MW installation is only a small part of the campus, but it puts the technology into operation at a live facility. Envision, however, plans an even larger deployment in the next construction phases, a move that aligns with Nvidia's push for 800V DC distribution in future high-density AI systems. Galaxy's campus uses a cooling arrangement in which liquid-cooled and air-cooled servers share a single water loop, eliminating the need for conventional central chiller plants. That matters as AI servers generate more heat and require increasingly sophisticated cooling systems. Removing central chillers can simplify infrastructure, although the design depends on local climate conditions and the facility's ability to reject heat through its water loop. China has previously experimented with other unconventional cooling methods, including a wind-powered underwater datacenter off Shanghai that uses surrounding seawater to help cool its servers. That said, Galaxy is the first major project in Invision's wider Inner Mongolia datacentre plans, which Semianalysis says add up to 3GW, with the rest of the campus still a busy construction site. The surrounding Chahar High-tech Zone is also expanding rapidly, with nearly 30,000 construction workers spread across 22 data center projects, according to a local report cited by the researchers. The wider Chinese expansion is also attracting some of the world's largest technology companies. Alibaba, Huawei and ByteDance are among the firms expanding infrastructure in the region, which benefits from relatively cheap electricity, available land and abundant wind resources. However access to electricity and datacenter buildings does not automatically translate to available AI computing power. China's access to advanced accelerators remains a separate constraint, particularly as US export restrictions limit its ability to acquire Nvidia ’s most powerful chips.

title: Jensen Huang Nvidia affair scandal: What we know, what we don’t
zh_title: 黄仁勋 Nvidia 事件丑闻：我们知道什么，我们不知道什么
summary: 周日，芯片制造商英伟达在其网站的新闻编辑室页面上发布了其创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋的奇怪新闻稿。标题为“给我们公司的一封信”的新闻稿也通过电子邮件发送给了公司的员工。 “我欠我的家人和你们所有人一个道歉。我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”领导着世界上最有价值公司之一的黄为什么要通过官方公司通讯分享这些个人信息？因为与他有染的女人被指控了
content:
周日，芯片制造商英伟达在其网站的新闻编辑室页面上发布了其创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋的奇怪新闻稿。标题为“给我们公司的一封信”的新闻稿也通过电子邮件发送给了公司的员工。 “我欠我的家人和你们所有人一个道歉。我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”领导着世界上最有价值公司之一的黄为什么要通过官方公司通讯分享这些个人信息？据《纽约时报》和《金融时报》报道，这是因为与他有染的女子被指控为中国充当间谍。这不仅仅是一个公共关系丑闻。由于黄仁勋是人工智能行业的领军人物，英伟达是人工智能热潮的算力主要供应商，加上中美之间的人工智能军备竞赛，黄仁勋事件也是一个国家安全问题。我们所知道的 《纽约时报》和《金融时报》周末报道称，黄仁勋与中国公民、新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）有染，该公司是 Nvidia 芯片的主要采购商。据媒体报道，美国情报机构认为黄爱丽已被中国国家安全部招募为间谍。我们。
据《纽约时报》报道，对 Alice Huang 的监视发现，她一直与一名美国公民保持定期沟通，该公民后来被确认为 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官 Jensen Huang。据报道，Megaspeed 高管希望 Nvidia 首席执行官游说特朗普政府放松芯片出口管制。据报道，黄确实这么做了。据《纽约时报》报道，这一发现被视为高度国家安全风险，以至于今年春天国务卿马可·卢比奥亲自帮助起草了一份机密备忘录，警告特朗普政府黄与一名为中国最高情报机构工作的间谍的关系。根据周日发布在 Nvidia 网站上的公司董事会声明，该公司表示“没有理由相信国家安全或 Nvidia 机密受到损害”。董事会还表示，已对双方关系以及发生和未发生的情况展开独立调查。美联社今天报道称，中国否认黄爱丽以间谍身份为其政府工作，称这些指控是“诽谤活动”。我们不知道的除了黄本人证实了这件事，以及据报道美国情报部门认为爱丽丝黄是中国政府的间谍之外，还有很多我们不知道的事情。我们仍然不知道黄仁勋对黄爱丽了解多少，也不知道他受到或没有受到影响的程度。
我们不知道 Nvidia 的首席执行官可能告诉了 Alice Huang 哪些信息（如果有的话）被泄露了。如果信息被交换，我们不知道什么信息被传递给了中国政府。此外，据《华尔街日报》报道，爱丽丝·黄目前的行踪完全未知。她最后一次被确认到过中国是在 2024 年，当时美国情报机构开始对她进行调查。据《华尔街日报》报道，两人 2025 年在一起的照片最近浮出水面。目前尚不清楚这一国际事件的潜在影响有多大。威尔·詹斯

【原文 English Original】
On Sunday, chipmaker Nvidia posted an odd press release from its founder and CEO Jensen Huang on its website's newsroom page. The press release, titled "A Message to Our Company," was also emailed to the company's employees. "I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." Why did Huang, who leads one of the most valuable companies in the world, share this personal information through official corporate communications? It's because the woman he had an affair with has been accused of working as a spy for China, according to reports from the New York Times and the Financial Times . And this goes beyond just a public relations scandal. With Huang being a leading figure in the AI industry, Nvidia being the major supplier of computing power for the AI boom, and the AI arms race between the U.S. and China, Huang's affair is also an issue of national security. What we know The New York Times and the Financial Times reported over the weekend that Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a Chinese citizen and top executive at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, a major purchaser of Nvidia's chips. According to the outlets, U.S. intelligence agencies believe that Alice Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security as a spy. U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang found that she had been in regular communication with an American citizen, who was later identified as Jensen Huang, the founder and CEO of Nvidia, according to the New York Times . The Megaspeed executive reportedly wanted the Nvidia CEO to lobby the Trump administration to loosen chip export controls. Huang reportedly did exactly that. This discovery was treated as such a high-level national security risk that Secretary of State Marco Rubio himself helped draft a classified memo this spring warning the Trump administration of Huang's relationship with a spy working for China’s top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported. The company said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised," per a statement from the company's board of directors  posted to the Nvidia website  on Sunday. The board also said that it had opened its own independent investigation into the relationship and what did and didn't occur. The Associated Press reported today that China has denied that Alice Huang works for its government as a spy, calling the accusations a "smear campaign." What we don't know Aside from the affair being confirmed by Huang himself, and U.S. intelligence reportedly believing that Alice Huang is a spy for the Chinese government, there's a lot that we don't know. We still don't know what Jensen Huang knew about Alice Huang, or to what degree he was or was not influenced. We don't know what Nvidia's CEO may have told Alice Huang and what information, if any, was compromised. If information was exchanged, we don't know what was passed to the Chinese government. In addition, Alice Huang's current whereabouts are completely unknown, according to the Wall Street Journal . She was last confirmed to have been in China in 2024, right around the time U.S. intelligence agencies began investigating her. Pictures from 2025 of the two together surfaced recently, according to the Wall Street Journal . It's unclear how wide the potential fallout of this international incident will be. Will Jensen Huang be indicted? Will he be forced to step down as CEO of Nvidia? If so, who is next in line to lead the California-based company, which has a current market cap of over $4.2 trillion ? content: ——当国家安全成为打压民主的工具 失去的将不仅是一个人的自由 从少年学生到民主运动的代表人物，从街头抗争到铁窗生涯，黄之锋的人生经历，折射出香港过去十多年来政治环境发生的巨大变化。资料图片。（孙明国／大纪元） 【大纪元2026年11月07日讯】2026年11月5日，香港民主运动人士、前香港众志秘书长黄之锋，被香港高等法院判处监禁10年。 这个消息令人震惊，也令人心痛。 一个年仅30岁的年轻人，从十几岁开始投身香港社会运动，经历了2014年的雨伞运动、2019年的反送中运动，最终却在自己人生最宝贵的青春岁月中，长期被关押在监狱里。 从少年学生到民主运动的代表人物，从街头抗争到铁窗生涯，黄之锋的人生经历，折射出香港过去十多年来政治环境发生的巨大变化。 这不仅仅是黄之锋一个人的悲剧，更是香港民主自由不断萎缩的历史缩影。 一、从雨伞运动到反送中：一代香港青年的民主理想 2014年，香港爆发雨伞运动。无数年轻人走上街头，要求真正的民主选举，要求香港人能够决定自己的未来。 当时的黄之锋还是一名年轻学生。他与许多香港青年一样，相信民主、自由、法治和公民权利，相信一个社会应当允许不同声音存在。 2019年，反送中运动再次席卷香港。 数以百万计的香港市民走上街头，表达对修订《逃犯条例》的担忧，也表达对香港自治、法治和自由前景的忧虑。 这场运动让全世界重新关注香港。 然而，运动之后，香港的政治环境发生了深刻变化。2020年6月30日，《香港国安法》实施，民主派组织相继解散，许多民主人士被捕、被起诉，新闻媒体和公民社会也受到巨大冲击。 香港曾经引以为傲的自由开放形象，正在发生根本性的变化。 二、十年刑期背后：国家安全与公民自由的冲突 根据中央社报导，黄之锋此次被控的罪名，是串谋勾结外国或者境外势力危害国家安全罪。 案件涉及他与罗冠聪等人，在2020年期间呼吁外国采取制裁等措施。 黄之锋此前已经因为香港民主派立法会初选案，被判处4年8个月监禁。此次又被判处10年。 值得注意的是，法院裁定其中2个月2日与原有刑期同期执行。 对于这一判决，我们不能只停留在法律条文和刑期数字上，更应该追问一个根本问题： 一个社会究竟应当如何界定国家安全？公民表达政治诉求、寻求国际社会关注，是否就应该被视为危害国家安全？ 国家安全固然重要，但国家安全不应成为无限扩大权力、压制公民基本权利的理由。 真正有信心的政府，应当允许社会批评，接受公众监督，尊重不同政治意见。 如果一个政府无法容忍批评，甚至将政治异见视为国家安全威胁，那么受到损害的，不只是个人自由，更是整个社会的法治基础。 三、香港的悲剧 是中共承诺与现实之间的巨大落差 香港回归之初，国际社会关注的核心问题之一，就是香港能否保持原有的生活方式和制度。 一国两制的承诺，曾经让香港人对未来抱有希望。 香港之所以能够成为国际金融中心，不仅因为它拥有优越的地理位置和经济条件，更因为它曾经拥有相对独立的司法制度、开放的信息环境、自由的新闻媒体以及受到保障的公民权利。 这些制度优势，是香港最宝贵的财富。 然而，当政治权力不断扩大，当新闻自由受到压缩，当民主人士因为政治活动而长期失去人身自由，香港原有的制度优势也必然受到冲击。 一个国际城市的竞争力，不能仅仅依靠高楼大厦、金融市场和经济数据来维持。 自由、法治、诚信和制度保障，同样是不可替代的基础。 失去这些，香港失去的将不仅是过去的光环，更可能是未来的国际信任。 四、压制可以让街头安静 却无法消灭人民对自由的向往 历史一再证明，强权可以控制一时的社会秩序，却无法永远控制人的思想。 香港民主运动经历了挫折，许多参与者被迫离开家园，有人身陷囹圄，有人流亡海外，也有人选择沉默。 但是，民主、自由和人权并不是某一个政治组织的专利，而是人类社会共同追求的基本价值。 黄之锋被判刑10年，令人看到一个年轻人的人生被长期监禁所改变，也让世界重新思考香港的自由究竟走向何方。 我们不应该因为一个人身陷囹圄，就认为他的理想也随之消失。 历史不会因为监狱的大门关闭，就停止记录一个时代的真相。 五、香港的今天 也应该成为中国未来的警示 香港曾经是中国与自由世界之间重要的桥梁。 它向世界证明，华人社会同样能够拥有自由、法治、民主和繁荣。 香港的民主运动，也让更多中国大陆民众看到，追求公民权利、要求政府接受监督，并不是所谓的西方专利，而是每一个现代社会公民都应当享有的权利。 今天香港所经历的一切，也值得中国大陆人民深思。 一个国家真正的强大，不是让所有人只说一种声音，而是能够容纳不同意见；不是让人民对权力保持恐惧，而是让权力接受人民监督。 一个政府的合法性和社会公信力，不应建立在恐惧和沉默之上，而应建立在人民的信任、法律的公正以及公民权利的保障之上。 香港的自由不能成为历史，中国的民主也不应该成为遥不可及的梦想。 黄之锋案再次提醒我们：民主的道路可能曲折，自由的代价有时沉重，但一个民族不能因为恐惧而放弃对尊严的追求。 十年铁窗，锁住的是一个人的身体，却不应该成为一个时代思想的牢笼。 对于香港，我们希望有一天能够重新拥有真正的新闻自由、司法独立、民主选举和公民权利。 对于中国，我们期待一个不再以政治恐惧统治人民、不再把不同声音视为敌人的民主社会。 自由不应当是罪名，民主不应当是禁忌，人权更不应当成为任何政权可以随意剥夺的东西。 这是黄之锋案留给香港、留给中国，也留给整个自由世界的一道严肃考题。

title: General Atomics Ranger UUV to Support Large Payloads, UAVs
zh_title: 通用原子公司 Ranger UUV 支持大型有效载荷、无人机
summary: 在 Euronaval 2026 上，通用原子公司展示了其 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 远程 UUV，专为多年任务以及发射子无人机和有效载荷而设计。通用原子公司 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 无人水下航行器将支持潜射无人机和广泛的有效载荷模块，以执行监视、采矿和打击任务。在 Euronaval 2026 上，《海军新闻》采访了 GA 电磁系统公司海事项目副总裁 Rolf Ziesing，了解通用原子公司的海底无人开发项目。 “我们对这个 UUV 项目感到非常兴奋。我们正在解决一个关键需求
content:
在 Euronaval 2026 上，通用原子公司展示了其 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 远程 UUV，专为多年任务以及发射子无人机和有效载荷而设计。通用原子公司 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 无人水下航行器将支持潜射无人机和广泛的有效载荷模块，以执行监视、采矿和打击任务。在 Euronaval 2026 上，《海军新闻》采访了 GA 电磁系统公司海事项目副总裁 Rolf Ziesing，了解通用原子公司的海底无人开发项目。 “我们对这个 UUV 项目感到非常兴奋。我们正在解决 UUV 领域的一个关键需求，即续航能力和任务范围。为了解决这些问题，我们开发了一种动力能源系统，使 UUV 能够运行多年或数万公里，”Ziesing 说。 Ziesing 解释说，该公司正在努力将概念工作扩大到 100 至 135 英尺长的 UUV，能够携带更多无人机和其他有效载荷。与传统的基于螺旋桨的推进方法相比，通用原子公司选择了浮力滑翔机设计来增加航程和耐力。 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 为此使用推进器和专门设计的控制面。 General Atomic 概念图强调了滑翔机型 UUV 使用冲绳和关岛发射点的射程。从这些基地位置，无人潜航器可以到达第一岛链的咽喉要道或中国大陆沿岸的水域。
“仅将关岛作为行动中心，我们正在考虑向西太平洋地区秘密运送一架飞行器以支持任务行动。相对于当今现有的 LDUUV 和 XLUUV，这种滑翔机的射程和到达范围要大几个数量级。这确实是一个关键需求，需要运送有效载荷并让平台长时间停留在驻地。” Rolf Ziesing，GA 电磁系统公司海事项目副总裁 通过该设计的增程部署和任务续航能力，Ziesing 强调了 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 可以携带的有效载荷的潜力。 “滑翔机船是可扩展的。我们现在有一艘 22 英尺长的两用船。我们现在用它来降低风险和概念开发。同时，它是部署这些小型 UUV 的有用平台。我们将把 22 英尺平台扩展到 100 英尺翼展平台，该平台将具有货运能力，相当于 CONEX 箱的大小。在该货舱中，可以携带各种有效载荷，”Ziesing 说。无人机、UUV 有效载荷通用原子公司潜射四轴飞行器无人机。 General Atomics 图形 通用原子公司正在利用这些较小的 UUV 开发各种功能和有效载荷。在 Euronaval 2026 上，通用原子公司展示了他们开发的潜射四轴飞行器无人机。
一段真实测试的视频显示了无人机从管道中的部署，该管道将从通过 Ranger 或 GA-Ray 部署的 UUV 发射。该无人机的规格尚未向海军新闻透露。 Ranger 和 GA-Ray 型 UUV 的图形表示根据变体的大小可以携带多少小型水下无人机。根据描述，有效载荷可以在 16 到 96 个子 UUV 之间变化。 “我们确实将其视为一个 UUV 系统。因此，我们有一个大型主机 UUV，旨在携带有效载荷。有效载荷是我们开发的另一艘 UUV，我们已经操作过这两种 UUV。

【原文 English Original】
At Euronaval 2026, General Atomics revealed its Ranger and GA-Ray long-range UUVs, built for multi-year missions and launching sub-drones and payloads. General Atomics Ranger and GA-Ray unmanned underwater vehicles will support submarine-launched drones and extensive payload modules to address surveillance, mining and strike missions. At Euronaval 2026, Naval News talked with Rolf Ziesing, Vice President of Maritime Programs at GA Electromagnetic Systems, to learn about General Atomics undersea unmanned developments. “We’re very excited with this UUV program. We’re addressing a critical need in the UUV space, which is endurance and mission reach. To solve those problems, we’ve developed a power energy system that will allow UUV to operate for multiple years or tens of thousands of kilometers,” said Ziesing. Ziesing explained that the company is working to scale up concept work into a 100 to 135-foot UUV capable of carrying additional drones and other payloads. Compared to traditional propeller-based propulsion methods, General Atomics opted for the buoyancy-derived glider design to increase range and endurance. Ranger and GA-Ray utilize thrusters and specially designed control surfaces for this purpose. A General Atomic concept graphics highlighted the range of the glider-type UUV using a launch point from Okinawa and Guam. From these basing locations, the UUVs can reach First Island Chain chokepoints or waters within the littorals of mainland China. “Just looking at Guam as a center of operation, we’re looking at delivering a vehicle covertly to the Western Pacific region to support mission operations. Relative to the existing LDUUV and XLUUV of today, the range and reach of this glider is orders and magnitude greater. That’s really a critical need, to deliver payload and have a platform stay on station for extended periods of time.” Rolf Ziesing, Vice President of Maritime Programs at GA Electromagnetic Systems Through the design’s extended-range deployment and mission endurance possibilities, Ziesing emphasized the potential of the payloads that can be carried by Ranger and GA-Ray. “The glider ship is scalable. We have a 22-foot vessel now that’s dual-purpose. We’re using it now for risk reduction and concept development. At the same time, its a useful platform to deploy these smaller UUVs. We will scale the 22-foot platform up to a 100-foot wingspan platform that will have cargo capacity – the equivalent size of a CONEX box. In that cargo bay, there is a variety of payloads that can be carried ,” said Ziesing. UAV, UUV Payloads General Atomics submarine-launched quadcopter UAV. General Atomics graphic From these smaller UUVs, General Atomics is developing a variety of capabilities and payloads. At Euronaval 2026, General Atomics showcased their development of a submarine-launched quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicle. A video of a real-life test shows the deployment of the UAV from a tube that will be launched from the UUV deployed via Ranger or GA-Ray. The specifications of this UAV were not disclosed to Naval News . A graphic of Ranger and GA-Ray type UUVs denotes how many of the smaller underwater drones can be carried depending on the size of the variant. According to the depiction, the payload can vary between 16 to 96 sub-UUVs. “We’re really looking at this as a system of UUVs. So we have a large host UUV, which is intended to carry the payload. The payload is another UUV that we have developed and we have operated both of these at-sea,” said Ziesing. Aside from the sub-UUVs, at least two large displacement drones of an unspecified variant or a containerized payload can also be deployed carried. “It can transport two large diameter UUVs that can then do their own missions. Or it can drop the CONEX box to remain on station. Or it can just sit at the bottom with the CONEX box, with the door that opens at the top, to deploy different payloads to deliver different types of effects,” said Ziesing. “It’s intended to deliver very large cargo payloads for a variety of missions. So it can stay on mission, stay covert and energize on command to support mission operations.” General Atomics previously showed a concept of maintaining an extended patrol of dual-sonar array equipped Ranger UUVs off the North American West Coast to protect the continental U.S. Ranger, GA-Ray Potential Amid New U.S. Navy Plans Ranger and GA-Ray notional operational ranges. General Atomics photos The American defense firm’s modular underwater gliders come amid new demands from the U.S. Navy’s Hedge Force Strategy. Debuted by Chief of Naval Operations Daryl Caudle at Surface Navy Association 2026, the sea service plans to combine unmanned systems with warships, aircraft and submarines to tailored “hedges” against specific adversaries. General Atomics claims that these UUVs can take on missions previously handled by nuclear attack boats and provide multi-month to multi-year on-station endurance to commanders. These include mining, surveillance and anti-submarine missions. Tests held to date include operations while submerged lasting up to 70 days to simulated the type of missions General Atomics anticipates for the drones. Going forward, Ziesing told Naval News that the company’s UUV work has attracted “many interested parties.” “There’s a lot of interest. The payloads we’re developing are very unique and novel. You can image that there are other payloads we are developing that we’re not going to talk about. And because of the ability to deliver these payloads covertly for extended periods of time, there’s a lot of interest.” The post General Atomics Ranger UUV to Support Large Payloads, UAVs appeared first on Naval News .

title: Europe needs Nvidia. It’ll take more than a spy scandal to change that.
zh_title: 欧洲需要英伟达。要改变这一现状，光靠间谍丑闻是不够的。

content:
布鲁塞尔——上个月，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋受到了查尔斯国王、法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙和德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨等人的欧洲全面红地毯待遇。现在是蟋蟀。随着全球主要人工智能微芯片生产商的经营者被指控的中国间谍丑闻席卷而来，与黄仁勋接触并签署协议的欧洲公共和私营部门领导人面临着潜在的尴尬问题。但这种沉默也反映出冷酷的经济和战略现实，即欧洲没有除英伟达之外的本土替代品。德国政府发言人周一在回应有关英伟达剧变的一系列问题时表示，“不会对媒体报道发表评论”，并且“我们始终坚持最高标准，包括在达成协议时”。欧盟委员会发言人也没有对此事发表评论。在硅谷和华盛顿，调查人员已经忙碌起来。在黄与一名涉嫌试图向北京输送美国芯片情报的中国女商人建立了密切关系后，英伟达已对其首席执行官是否成为中国情报部门的目标展开内部调查。黄某已公开承认有外遇。美国国会，尤其是对中国持警惕态度的派系，也准备采取行动。 “美国
众议院外交事务委员会前主席、得克萨斯州共和党众议员迈克尔·麦考尔 (Michael McCaul) 表示：“美国应该立即暂停向中国运送先进的人工智能芯片，直到我们查清这起事件的真相，并确保我们的国家安全不会受到损害。”在布鲁塞尔，对于那些警告美国科技在人工智能竞赛中占据主导地位的人来说，对这家硅谷巨头的打击似乎是个好消息。但与最近中期选举的结果一样，英伟达的困境也不容忽视。欧盟最新芯片制造计划的谈判代表之一、荷兰欧洲议会议员巴特·格鲁特修斯 (Bart Groothuis) 表示，“我们没有任何替代方案，芯片的设计几乎完全是美国的”。欧洲对 Nvidia 的严重依赖在黄仁勋 10 月份的欧洲之旅中得到了体现，其中包括接受查尔斯国王颁发的奖牌并与德国梅尔茨同台表演。过去一年，欧盟高管也一直在排队：欧盟创新主管叶卡捷琳娜·扎哈里耶娃(Ekaterina Zaharieva)今年春天在访问美国时会见了黄仁勋；根据欧盟透明度登记册中的一项记录，欧盟科技主管 Henna Virkkunen 和内阁成员在 9 月份讨论了数字沙皇和黄仁勋之间“可能的会面”，这次会议也将探讨 Nvidia 在欧洲的投资。委员会拒绝就该会议现在是否已取消发表评论。
不可或缺 在布鲁塞尔，受到投资追捧的美国科技高管已经不多了。但英伟达对于欧洲在全球人工智能竞赛中保持领先地位的努力不可或缺，因为其强大的芯片对于训练欧洲渴望拥有的复杂而先进的模型是必要的。当即将卸任的拜登政府于 2025 年初限制向一系列欧盟国家出口人工智能芯片时，布鲁塞尔猛然意识到了这一现实，引发了整个欧盟的外交争夺。此后，欧盟将自己描绘成美国人工智能芯片的愿意买家，最终达到了顶峰。

【原文 English Original】
BRUSSELS — Last month, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang got Europe’s full red-carpet treatment from the likes of King Charles, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Now it’s crickets. As an alleged Chinese spy scandal engulfs the man running the world’s dominant AI microchips producer, potentially awkward questions loom for European leaders in both the public and private sectors who rubbed shoulders and inked deals with Huang. But the silence also reflects the cold economic and strategic reality that Europe has no homegrown alternative to Nvidia. A German government spokesperson said Monday in response to a barrage of questions on the upheaval at Nvidia that it “does not comment on the media reports,” and that “we always adhere to the highest standards, including when agreements are being reached.” A European Commission spokesperson also had no comment on the matter. In both Silicon Valley and Washington, investigators are already busy. Nvidia has opened an internal investigation into whether its CEO was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation, after Huang developed an intimate relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of trying to funnel intel on U.S. chips to Beijing. Huang has admitted publicly to having an affair. The U.S. Congress, particularly its factions wary of China, is also set to take action. “The U.S. should immediately pause the shipment of advanced AI chips to China until we can get to the bottom of this incident and ensure our national security is not being undermined,” Rep. Michael McCaul, a Republican from Texas, and former chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said on X . In Brussels, the blow to the Silicon Valley giant might appear to be good news for those who warn of U.S. tech dominance in the AI race. But as with the recent results of the midterm elections, the woes at Nvidia don’t change Europe’s reality because the bloc is so reliant on the company’s AI chips. “We don’t have any alternative, the design [of chips] is almost entirely U.S.,” said Dutch European Parliament lawmaker Bart Groothuis, one of the negotiators of the bloc’s latest chipmaking plan. Groothuis decried Nvidia’s “bizarre monopoly position.” Europe’s heavy reliance on Nvidia was on display during Huang’s October tour through Europe, which included receiving a medal from King Charles and sharing a stage with Germany’s Merz. EU executives have been lining up over the past year as well: EU innovation chief Ekaterina Zaharieva met Huang on a trip to the U.S. this spring ; and Cabinet members of EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen discussed in September a “possible meeting” between the digital czar and Huang, per an entry in the EU’s transparency register, which would also explore Nvidia investments in Europe. The Commission declined to comment on whether that meeting is now off the table. Indispensable Being courted for investments is a status that not many U.S. tech executives still enjoy in Brussels. But Nvidia made itself indispensable to Europe’s efforts to keep up in the global artificial intelligence race since its powerful chips are necessary to train the complex and advanced models that Europe aspires to have. Brussels was jolted awake to that reality when the outgoing Biden administration limited AI chip exports to a series of EU countries in early 2025, which triggered a diplomatic scramble across the bloc. Since then, the EU has portrayed itself as a willing buyer of American AI chips, culminating in the EU’s promise to buy €40 billion of the chips as part of the EU-U.S. trade deal. When the European Commission began an effort to build seven massive AI compute hubs at the end of July, an investment worth €30 billion, Nvidia was one of the three U.S. companies that were selected “to ensure … seamless access to necessary hardware.” The bloc has only recently begun efforts to wean off its reliance on U.S. advanced chips through a new chipmaking plan it presented in June. That plan warned that the bloc is almost “entirely dependent on the United States and Asia for the most advanced and leading-edge chips … including AI chips” and pitched an EU-based advanced chips factory as a strategic project “with the highest priority.” It’s not even necessary to plough billions into a factory. Nvidia itself doesn’t manufacture chips, it designs them — and then relies on companies such as Taiwan-based TSMC to produce them. This all raises the stakes for Europe to become a force in chip design, a craft Nvidia has mastered over the years and that has made it the world’s most valuable company. “The entry to that market is quite accessible, the knowledge to do better is also available in Europe,” Groothuis quipped.

参议员就中国之行拷问辩方证人
2026 年 11 月 10 日 | 12:00 上午
达沃市评估员海梅·阿达林 (Jaime Adalin) 在回答参议员里萨·洪蒂维罗斯 (Risa Hontiveros) 关于他在 2026 年 1 月中国之行期间访问过的地点的问题时表示，在 2026 年 11 月 9 日弹劾审判的第 40 天期间，他已无法回忆起这些地点。
菲律宾马尼拉——令参议员法官们愤怒的是，副总统萨拉·杜特尔特(Sara Duterte)弹劾审判昨天恢复进行时，一名辩方证人一再声称不记得他10个月前访问中国的细节，即使是在受到藐视法庭警告之后也是如此。
当检察官杰伊·托洛萨（Jay Tolosa）要求他确认最近是否去过中国时，达沃市评估员杰米·阿达林（Jaime Adalin）声称他一开始不记得有过这样的旅行，但后来承认确实有过一次，他今年早些时候与其他市政府部门负责人一起去过中国。
阿达林因 2026 年 1 月前往北京和上海的旅行以及杜特尔特财产申报价值的明显差异而受到严厉拷问。
当阿达林最初声称他不记得自己去了中国的哪些地方，也不记得是谁组织了这次旅行时，参议员里萨·洪蒂维罗斯表示难以置信。
“先生，我很抱歉 po, 印度语 po talaga nakakatawa（这真的不好笑），”她微笑着告诉阿达林。
她说：“令人难以置信的是，一名工程师、一名城市评估员可以阅读辩方和检方提供的地图，却无法回忆起自己去过的哪个大国。”
阿达林解释说，他“不热衷于旅行”，也没有记住自己的行程。
不过，他证实，与他同行的还有城市工程师、城市财务主管和城市管理员，并强调这是一次“个人旅行”，他们自己支付费用。
当洪蒂维洛斯追问他于1月25日进入北京并于1月30日经上海出境的确切航班信息时，阿达林回答说，该信息“很可能”是正确的。
参议员欧文·图尔福警告阿达林，他可能会因回避和嘲笑法庭而被视为藐视法庭。
参议员拉菲·图尔福 (Raffy Tulfo) 还在 2018 年 11 月早些时候的一次中国之行中对阿达林提出了质询，强调了与杜特尔特丈夫马纳塞斯·卡皮奥 (Manases Carpio) 有关的一家公司收到来自中国和香港的 3.19 亿比索汇入汇款的指控。
他说：“如果菲律宾人发现一名官员、一名高级官员正在接受来自与我们在西菲律宾海发生冲突的中国的资金，那就不好听了。”
众议院检察官众议员蔡乔尔指责阿达林满口谎言。 “我们可以看出，他们的第一个证人是个骗子，他甚至想在我们身上放一个证人，”马尼拉第三区议员指出。
阿达林试图确定达沃市的一处有产权财产与杜特尔特在资产、负债和净值宣誓声明中申报的财产相同。他依赖于其描笼涯的位置以及匹配的评估价值和公平市场价值。
对于南拉瑙市众议员齐亚·阿隆托·阿迪翁 (Zia Alonto Adiong) 来说，阿达林未能证明杜特尔特丈夫名下登记的财产在她的 SALN 中得到了适当披露。
“现在可以肯定的是，他们的证人在试图向法庭和人民证明副总统一直与她的主张一致方面惨遭失败。

Senators grill defense witness over China trip
November 10, 2026 | 12:00am
Davao City assessor Jaime Adalin responds to Sen. Risa Hontiveros’ questions about the places he visited during his January 2026 trip to China, saying he could no longer recall the locations, during the 40th day of the impeachment trial on November 9, 2026.
MANILA, Philippines — To senator-judges’ exasperation, a defense witness at the resumption yesterday of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte repeatedly claimed not recalling details of his trip to China made just 10 months ago, even after being warned of contempt.
Asked by prosecutor Jay Tolosa to confirm if he had traveled to China recently, Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin claimed at first he could not remember such a trip, but later admitted there was one indeed which he took with other city department heads early this year.
Adalin was subjected to intense grilling over his January 2026 travel to Beijing and Shanghai, as well as over apparent discrepancies in the declared values of Duterte’s properties.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros expressed disbelief when Adalin initially claimed he could not recall where in China he traveled to, or who organized the trip.
“Sir, I’m sorry po, hindi po talaga nakakatawa (it’s really not funny),” she told Adalin, who was smiling.
“It’s unbelievable that an engineer, a city assessor, who can read maps presented by the defense and the prosecution, can’t recall a big country he had been to,” she said.
Adalin explained that he is “not keen on traveling” and did not memorize his itinerary.
He confirmed, however, that he was joined by the city engineer, city treasurer and city administrator, stressing that it was a “personal travel” and that they paid for their own expenses.
When pressed by Hontiveros with exact flight details indicating he entered Beijing on Jan. 25 and exited via Shanghai on Jan. 30, Adalin replied the information was “most probably” correct.
Sen. Erwin Tulfo warned Adalin that he could be cited in contempt for being evasive and making a mockery of the court.
Sen. Raffy Tulfo also questioned Adalin on an earlier China trip in November 2018, highlighting allegations that a company linked to Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio received P319 million in inward remittances from China and Hong Kong.
“Not good to hear, if the Filipinos would find out that an official, a high ranking official, is receiving money from China with whom we are in conflict over the West Philippine Sea,” he said.
House prosecutor Rep. Joel Chua accused Adalin of lying through his teeth. “We can see that their first witness is a liar, and he even wants to put one over us,” the third district congressman of Manila pointed out.
Adalin sought to establish that a titled property in Davao City was the same property declared in Duterte’s sworn statement of assets, liabilities and net worth. He relied on its barangay location and on matching assessed and fair market values.
For Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, Adalin failed to establish that a property registered under Duterte’s husband was properly disclosed in her SALN.
“What is certain now is that their witness failed miserably in trying to prove to the court and to the people that the Vice President has been consistent with her declaration,” Adiong said at a press conference.
Adiong also questioned the consistency of Adalin’s testimony. “Their witness is inconsistent,” the chairman of the House committee on suffrage and electoral reforms said.
The disputed records included a P6-million selling-price entry in the electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration and a P10-million acquisition cost reflected in Duterte’s 2024 SALN.
The prosecution also pointed to differences between the property’s description as a lot with improvements and as residential-lot entry presented during the questioning.
Asked by Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian how sure he was that the Carpio Matina property is the residential lot declared in Duterte’s SALN, Adalin said he merely based it on the same assessed value of P82,046 as well as on the tax declarations.
Sen. Francis Pangilinan said he found it hard to believe the witness’ claim that the Carpio Matina property is the same as that declared in the SALN just based on the deed of sale.
He flagged the witness’ conflicting claims about the property in light of the prosecution’s revelation that the property turned out to be a commercial food establishment.
“Clearly, there are inconsistencies in your testimonies. Forgive me, engineer, but you say one thing and then you say another thing, so we are wondering: ano ba talaga ang totoo sa sinasabi mo,” he added.
At a press briefing after the hearing, defense spokesman Michael Poa said Adalin was able to prove that the property in Davao City was declared in Duterte’s SALN.
“We laid down the facts, we asked the city assessor for his personal opinion, because that is his job, we just leave it to the appreciation of the impeachment court,” Poa said. — Neil Jayson Servallos, Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Bella Cariaso
